items.name: The Sun's Design
items.description: A scorched slab of black corundum, minutely scratched on every side with intricate ideoglyphs. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 一块烧焦的黑刚玉石板，每一面都细致入微地雕刻了复杂的象形文字。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: In the city of Emesa, beneath the Church of the Holy Belt, in a sarcophagus of black corundum, Elagabalus lies: accursed of Janus, neither Long nor mortal, neither man nor woman, neither a liar nor a speaker of truth, neither real nor imagined. On his light-suffused skin is made manifest the Sun-in-Splendour's grand design...
readings.content: Elagabalus is the source of one-half of this text. The source of the other-half is obscure, but its power is evident. It is impossible to be certain if the Sun really planned for us to enter Eternity. It is impossible to be sure if the Grail, the Vagabond, and the Forge, stole this birthright from us, or saved us from it. But there is a great secret here.

readings_cn.content: 埃拉伽巴路斯只是本篇的一半来源。另一半来源模糊不清，但其中的力量显而易见。无法确定骄阳是否真的曾计划过让我们迈入永恒。也无法确定圣杯、浪游旅人和铸炉究竟是偷走了我们与生俱来的权利，还是将我们从中拯救。但其中蕴含着一个伟大的秘密。
readings_cn.intro: 埃美萨的城墙内，圣带教堂的穹顶下，黑色刚玉的石棺中，长眠着埃拉伽巴路斯：被雅努斯诅咒者，既非长生也非凡人，既非男人也非女人，既非说谎者也非真言者，既非真实也非幻想。他洋溢着光芒的皮肤上彰显着骄阳的宏图……

results.result_name: Numen: the Paths of the Sun

items.name: The Sun Disfigured
items.description: A scroll of anthropoderm parchment, written in the golden ink called Uzult. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 一本人皮书卷，用被称作珀金的金色墨水写就。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: The author of the text calls herself 'the Elagabaline'. Sometimes she seems to be Sunset Celia, the Watchman's Name; sometimes she seems to be Lady Tryphon, the Grail-long. It is unclear whether these are separate entities or the same person - it may be unclear even to the writer.
readings.content: The flaws in the Sun's Plan are elucidated. The Sun's Plan itself is never entirely clear, but it is a project of some kind to enter, possess, or surrender to the Glory - the pure light above the Mansus. This book suggests ways in which that Plan might fail.

readings_cn.intro: 本卷的作者自称“埃拉伽巴路斯氏”。有时她看上去像是守夜人的具名者，日落西莉亚；有时她又像是杯之长生者，特里丰女士。尚不清楚她们是不同的存在还是同一个体——也许作者本人也不能确定。
readings_cn.content: 本卷阐明了太阳的宏图之缺陷。太阳的宏图本身从未明晰，但那是一个期以进入、占有或屈服于辉光的计划——那凌驾于漫宿之上的纯净光芒。本书指出了其可能会失败的一些情况。

items.name: Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic
items.description: Or, 'The House of Glass'. Julian Coseley considered this his masterwork. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 又名“镜之居屋”。朱利安·科赛利称本书为他的杰作。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: Techniques for perception and analysis which permit invidious and apocalyptic conclusions. Probably the most assiduously suppressed book in history. The entire run was destroyed - even the presses were melted and dispersed - but the manuscript edition has survived.
readings.content: The perfect hegemony of the Hours is, perhaps, eternal. But Coseley proposes and describes 'Confinement Inescapable', aesthetic and optical techniques which might contain even an Hour, profoundly disrupting the order of the Mansus. He presents this as his own work, but there are hints here and there that he received inspiration or even assistance from the Nowhere-Hour named Snow.

readings_cn.content: 众司辰的完美霸权或许是永恒的。但是科赛利提出并描述了“勿逆囹圄”：一系列美学和光学技术，甚至可能做到禁锢一位司辰，这严重地威胁了漫宿的秩序。他声称本书是自己的作品，但书中的种种迹象都表明，他曾从名为白雪的虚界司辰那里得到过灵感、甚至是直接的协助。
readings_cn.intro: 本书阐述了关于感知与分析的技巧，从中可以得出令人反感且预示着大灾变的结论。可能是历史上被查禁得最严格的书籍之一。所有的印刷本都被销毁——就连印刷机也难逃熔化与拆解的命运——但手抄版却幸存了下来。

items.name: Towards a Fundamental Aesthetic: Second Edition
items.description: Or, 'The Refinements of Light'. Julian Coseley had never wanted or expected to write a second edition of his masterwork... [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 又名“光之精炼”。朱利安·科赛利从未希望或预料过要给自己的杰作写第二版……[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: Julian Coseley long regarded Solomon Husher as a charlatan. But his friend Nina Lagasse painted three paintings before her death in 1895… and these paintings apparently convinced Coseley to change his mind. With considerable irritation, he revised his magnum opus.
readings.content: The perfect hegemony of the Hours is, perhaps, eternal. Coseley had always championed History rather than Eternity - the exceptions, limitations, contradictions of freedom. But Husher's and Lagasse's work convinced him to believe in the 'paradox of the eternal ending', a means in which perfection might be reconciled with freedom. He's not happy about it. This is perhaps the angriest book ever written in support of a peaceful philosophy of acceptance. But Coseley was always scrupulous about his conclusions.

readings_cn.intro: 朱利安·科赛利曾一直认为认为所罗门·赫舍是个江湖骗子。但他的朋友宁娜·拉格斯在1895年去世前留下了三幅画……这些画作显然说服科赛利改变了看法。他相当恼火地修改了自己的杰作。
readings_cn.content: 众司辰的完美霸权或许是永恒的。科赛利总是更愿意捍卫历史而非永恒——自由的例外、限制与矛盾。但是赫舍和拉格斯的研究结果使他不得不转而相信“永恒终结的悖论”，一种能使完美与自由达成和解的途径。他对此并不乐见。在支持平和容忍的哲学书籍中，这可能是有史以来最为愤懑的那本。但是科赛利对自己的结论向来不徇私情。

items.name: The Writing on the Wall
items.description: The most delicious traditions of the Carapace Cross, as recorded on the walls of the Mansus and transcribed into a book of ninety-nine pages by one known only as 'cc'. Although this book does not exist, it is read to a sleeper under certain very specific circumstances - and certain fragments jotted down on waking. [This 'book' houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 介壳种最为可口的传承，记录在漫宿的墙上，并被一个仅知其名为“cc”的人抄写在一本九十九页的书里。虽然这本书并不实际存在，但沉睡之人能在某些非常特殊的情况下读到它——且在醒时能草草记下某些段落。[这本“书”中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: 'It was Hunger that made Worms of Dragons - when they consumed the corpses of Hours. Without the savour-secret of the Carapace, their hunger would not have been sufficient…'
readings.content: Here is outlined the savour-secret of the Carapace, which harnesses hunger to permit impossible hybridisations. With this secret, even the most potent and fundamental entities have devoured and been devoured. And this, no doubt, is why it's secret.

readings_cn.intro: “当巨龙吞噬司辰的尸身之际，正是此等饥饿使它们蜕化为了蠕虫。要是没有介壳种的滋味之秘，它们的饥饿将永不满足……”
readings_cn.content: 本文概述了介壳种的滋味之秘，其利用饥饿使不可能的杂合成为可能。凭此秘密，即使最强大与最根本的存在也可以吞噬与被吞噬。毫无疑问，这就是为什么它是秘密。

items.name: A Child's Treasury of Golden Afternoons
items.description: Once upon a time, a very bad man encoded very bad secrets into the charming illustrations of a book of charming stories. Wake the pictures, and you will see. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 很久很久以前，有一个十足的坏蛋把十足的邪恶秘密编进了一本迷人的故事书的迷人插画里。唤醒插图，你将得见。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: Lord Jacob Gristwood: surgeon, ethnologist, philanthropist. There is no proof that he ever kept children in hutches beneath his bed. There is no proof he vivisected cats at dinner with his pen-knife. The Suppression Bureau keeps its secrets.
readings.content: 'Here is your paint,' whispered the Wolf to the Pale Girl. 'Here is your knife-for-scraping. And here is your face.'

readings_cn.intro: 雅各布·格里斯伍德勋爵：外科医生、人种学者、慈善家。没有证据表明他曾经把孩子们关在自己床底的笼子里。没有证据表明他曾经在晚餐时用削笔刀解剖活猫。防剿局的保密工作一向出色。
readings_cn.content: “这是你的颜料，”狼对苍白女孩耳语，“这是你的刮刀。这是你的脸蛋。”

items.name: Kopralith Omphalos
items.description: What is this? A tufted fossil of silken fibre, big as a child. [This object houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 这是什么？一块丝质纤维的簇状化石，像孩童一般大。[这件物品中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: Something consumed, and something was consumed. If we interpret its interweavings, we might understand.
readings.content: The meaning of this object isn't something that one reads, but rather something that one follows, until at last one has passed three times around it, and one finds the meaning waiting at one's shoulder.

readings_cn.content: 此物的真意无法解读，而是靠践行得出。在冥思苦想，绕其三圈之后，才蓦然发现其秘密就待在自己的肩头。
readings_cn.intro: 某物曾吞噬，某物曾被吞噬。如果我们能翻译其中交错的编织，兴许才能将它理解。

items.name: The Turquoise Hand
items.description: A calligraphic manual of Ramsund which employs as exemplar-text Farid ud-Din's 'Conference of the Birds'. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 拉姆桑德语的书法手册，采用法立德丁的《众鸟集会》作为范本。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: 'At noon the Sun moves like the beating of a wing. At sunset he sends the herald-child with her candle. At midnight, he sends the wind that extinguishes the candle-flame…'
readings.content: Commentary, illustrations and interleavings carry revelations never intended in the original: a sense of history, and the senses of Histories.

readings_cn.intro: “正午时分，太阳如振翅般行进。日落时分，他派来秉烛的年幼女使节。午夜时分，他送来寒风吹熄烛焰……”
readings_cn.content: 本书的注释、插图和穿插的文字揭示了原著中从未设想过的启迪：对历史的看法，对诸史的看法。

items.name: The Sky in the Scar
items.description: Gnomic exhortations that might be described as 'emergency procedures' for the return of the travelling kinds of the Carapace Cross. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 精辟入里的警言，或可形容成应对介壳种的远行诸族回归的“紧急手段”。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: Each page of this book except the last bears a single sign, clear and irrefutable as a gem...
readings.content: …the final page is empty. The travelling kinds of the Carapace Cross might never return.

readings_cn.intro: 除去最后一页，这本书的每一页上都有着一个独特的记号，如宝石般明澈动人而无可辩驳……
readings_cn.content: ……最后一页空空荡荡。介壳种的远行诸族也许永无归期。

items.name: Shuritic Book of Suns
items.description: A radically different text from any of the other versions of the Book of Suns, attributed to Hagar, Queen of Shur, Mother of Wolves. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 书中的文本与其他版本的《骄阳之书》有根本上的不同，其作者据信是夏甲，书珥女王，群狼之母。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: 'Set down with reverence before the Intercalate, by one who understood what would come to pass…'
readings.content: Apocryphal chapters foretell the means by which the Sun-in-Splendour and the Forge might circumvent the impossibility of their joining, through proxies that are in some sense themselves…

readings_cn.intro: “一位知晓何事将应验者，于置闰前满怀敬畏地记下此文……”
readings_cn.content: 杜撰的章节中预言了骄阳与铸炉或许会采用的手段：通过从某些角度看正是祂们自身的代理人，规避祂们无法结合的命运……

items.name: Amiranis Beteli
items.description: A fragment of iron-alloy meteorite carefully inscribed and polished. [This object houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 一块铁合金陨石的碎片，经过精心雕写和打磨。[这件物品中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: 'Who gave us fire? Who gave us steel? What is the sound of dusk? Of what alloy is wind forged?'
readings.content: Esoteric secrets of metallurgy and resonance are revealed - including directions towards the creation of a terrible Bell.

readings_cn.content: 铭文揭示了冶金与共振的机密——内含铸造一口令人敬畏之钟的指南。
readings_cn.intro: “谁予我们火？谁予我们钢？黄昏之声为何？风又以何种合金铸造？”

items.name: Serpent-Root
items.description: A mass of root-stock, shiny with age but still somehow viable. Tiny spidery scratchings, marked with embedded egg-shell shards, encode a cryptic message. [This object houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 一团粗壮的根须，随年岁增长而熠熠闪光，但不知为何仍保有生机。蜘蛛网般的细小划痕被镶嵌的蛋壳碎片所标注，编码了一个隐晦的秘密。[这件物品中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: Sea-born, tide-drawn, Meniscate-sister, Witch-lover. The House of the Moon will always have its messenger, though its messenger is different each time, in eye and flesh and heart…'
readings.content: Feits, feats, posterns, loopholes, set down against the advent of Eternity by powers favouring imperfection and impermanence.

readings_cn.intro: “海诞者，潮逐者，弧月的姐妹，女巫的情人。月亮的居屋每次都会派出它的使者，但每次的使者从眼睛到肉体到心灵都不尽相同……”
readings_cn.content: 事实，事迹，边门，罅隙：是那些偏爱瑕疵与无常的力量制定了它们，以对抗永恒的降临。

items.name: The Three and the Three (St Chiavi Manuscript)
items.description: This book describes the operations of the Chancel and the Calyptra, two triads of Hours with subtle, far-reaching powers and responsibilities. Of all the extant versions, this one has best survived the interventions of the Calyptra. [This book houses a numen - a truth so powerful it can perhaps believe itself.]
items.description_cn: 本书描述了圣坛和根冠的运作方式。它们分别由三位司辰组成，有着隐晦而广泛的权力和责任。现存的版本中，唯独这个版本免于根冠的干预，保存得最好。[这本书中寄宿着一个闰识——这个真理如此强大，或许它都相信自己可以被实现。]

readings.intro: 'Certain knowledge cannot be learnt by any entity below the rank of Know - outside the covenant of the Watchman's Tree. The enforcement of this rule is Calyptra. The three who enforce it are Calyptra also. It is said that Janus elects Calyptra, that the Chancel is the judgement of Janus, that Janus is the wound in the Law...'
readings.content: 'The Watchman's Tree is a compromise. If Calyptra could end it, they would. If the Watchman could end Calyptra, he might. Between their planes conflicting, sparks illuminate the angles of unmade law…'

readings_cn.intro: “在守夜人之树的盟约外，任何低于通晓者的存在都无法学习某些知识。这项律法的执行被称作根冠，而执行这律法的三者亦是根冠。据说是雅努斯挑选了根冠的人选，而圣坛是雅努斯的判决，雅努斯则是法则上的伤口……”
readings_cn.content: “守夜人之树是妥协的产物。如果根冠能终结它，那么根冠当然会这么做。如果守夜人能终结根冠，那么守夜人或许会这么做。在他们相互冲突的平面间，火花照亮了尚无法则管辖的角度……”

items.name: The Locksmith's Dream: Stolen Reflections
items.description: The fourth volume of Teresa Galmier's expansive work - no longer a discussion of the dreams of artisans, but a valuable survey of other works. The tone is calmer than that of 'Trespasses', but occasionally fearful, even paranoid. This volume was published in 1926 but almost immediately recalled and pulped by the publisher - at the request of the author or possibly the authorities, depending which story you believe. A few copies survive.
items.description_cn: 特蕾莎·加尔米耶所著的卷帙浩繁之作的第四卷——不再是关于匠人梦境的探讨，而是贵重的对其他职业的调查。笔锋相较《罪行》平静了许多，却时而透出惧意，甚至偏执。本卷于1926年出版，却几乎立刻就被出版社召回销毁——依作者或是政府的要求，随你相信哪种说法。只有数本得以保全。

readings.intro: 'Janus is the Gatekeeper, the twin-god, the god that wounds, the presager of changes, the sun, the moon. So we identify him with the Watchman, the Twins, with the Mother, with the Forge, with the Meniscate and the Madrugad. He cannot be all these. Can he? The flamines knew the Church, knew the Dry Land, knew Elagabalus. Is he then synthesis? Or is he something else? In Gallaecia they called him Ianus Lamius, but the Obliviates are notorious for their slanders.'
readings.content: 'Janus has, they say, not one face but two. To which I reply: why only one? Why only two? Hersault and Coseley - according to Thomas Love Denman - once agreed that Janus was 'all the gods and none'. But later, Hersault described him as 'all the gods', and Coseley favoured 'none'. Denman was a sinister dilettante, but this rings true of them both.'

readings_cn.intro: “雅努斯是守门者、双面之神、制造伤口之神、昭示改变之神，是太阳，是月亮。所以我们视他作守夜人、孪生子、蚁母、铸炉、弧月和昕旦。他不可能兼为上述诸神吧？这可能吗？古罗马祭司们了解教堂，了解干涸之地，了解埃拉伽巴路斯。所以他是杂糅而成的吗？亦或他是其他存在？在加拉埃西亚，人们称他为亚努斯·拉弥俄斯，不过忘却会是人尽皆知地爱好诽谤，此名不可全信。”
readings_cn.content: “那些人说，雅努斯不只有一张，而是有两张脸孔。对此我要回问：为何只有一张脸？为何只有两张脸？海索与朱利安——据托马斯·洛夫·登曼称——曾经认同‘此诸神兼是亦兼非’雅努斯。但在之后，海索坚称‘兼是’他，科赛利则偏爱单纯的‘兼非’。登曼是个不怀好意的半吊子，但这两种说法听起来各具其实。”

items.name: The Locksmith's Dream: Incursus
items.description: The fifth (and final?) volume of Teresa Galmier's notorious work, which began as an examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans but became an account of her own occult journey. This volume was apparently never published nor, allegedly, even written. Yet here it is.
items.description_cn: 特蕾莎·加尔米耶所著的臭名昭著之作的第五卷（及最后一卷？），始于作者对匠人们神秘梦境中的相似之处的考察，后来变成她自己探索密教之旅的笔记。这一卷显然从未出版过，而且据说，还没写出来。然而它已经在这了。

readings.intro: 'The Law goes back all the way to Stone: the Keys cannot be held or owned. This had, I believe, the unexpected consequence that those outside the law may hold and own them. But even they cannot keep them. And of course a Key is no more physical than a spirit. But a spirit may be housed in a body, and I have touched a Key with my own hands.'
readings.content: 'So the Ligeians hold the keys. I had thought the Ligeians only - 'only' - old and powerful transgressors of the Crime of the Sky. But I begin to understand that the Crime of the Sky is more even than it seems. And why a Twin, who unites what is not to be divided, might accept a Ligeian as her Name...'

readings_cn.content: “是以丽姬亚持有钥匙。我原以为丽姬亚只是——‘只是’——古老而强大的犯天孽者。但我开始明白，天孽比它看上去的意味着更多。以及为什么弥合不可分离之物的孪生子，会接受一位丽姬亚成为她的具名者……”
readings_cn.intro: “该法则可以追溯到石之时代：钥匙无法被持握或占有。我相信这反而导致了意想不到的结果——那些法则者之外或许能够持握与占有钥匙。但即使她们也无法将其长留。当然，钥匙并不比灵体更有形。但就连灵体也可以驻留在躯壳中，而我已经用自己的双手触碰过一把钥匙。”

items.name: The Fallen Cross
items.description: In which Julian Coseley, magus, immortal, occasional anarchist, argues that through language the Carapace Cross decayed to seed the lives of our ancestors.
items.description_cn: 术士，不朽者，偶尔还是无政府主义者的朱利安·科赛利，在本书中认为：通过语言，介壳种衰落，播撒下我们祖先的种子。

readings.intro: 'Speech is a Wound; Silence is Silver. There is no Silver Door, nor can there be, even in the Moon's House…'
readings.content: 'Without Language there can be no Wordes. Without Wordes there can be no Message. But only in Silence can there be no Error; and Lo, even in that beginning, in that First of Messages, an Error. Thus did we enter the House.'

readings_cn.intro: “言辞是伤口；沉默是白银。世上没有，也不可能有白银之门，即便是在月亮的居屋中也是如此……”
readings_cn.content: “无语言则无言辞。无言辞则无信息。唯有沉默中方无谬误；看呐，即便在万物伊始，在那初成的信息中也有谬误。我们藉此进入了居屋。”

items.name: Kitling Ripe and the Moldywarp's Grave (and Other Stories)
items.name_cn: 《老成仔猫与鼹鼠的坟墓（及其他故事）》
items.description: A lusciously illustrated tome of loosely connected children's stories. Few of them are remotely suitable for children.
items.description_cn: 一本插图华美的大书，内含数篇关联松散的儿童故事。这些故事没有几篇适合儿童阅读。

readings.intro: The protagonist, a speechless cat-thing called Kitling Ripe, performs a series of elaborate rites to rescue members of her extended family, culminating in the resurrection of her 'other grandmother', Moldywarp.
readings.content: 'When the Snake-Witch killed the horse, Kitling snatched one of its eyes. When the Dry-Witch killed the pig, Kitling stole a cup of its blood. Then she took them to the place Moldywarp lay buried, and she shook out her hair, and she began to dance…'

readings_cn.content: “蛇女巫杀死牡鹿时，仔猫抠出了它一只眼睛。干涸女巫杀死牝猪时，仔猫偷去了它一杯血液。随后她带着这些东西到埋葬鼹鼠的地方，散开自己的头发，开始舞蹈……”
readings_cn.intro: 本书主角，一只名为老成仔猫的无言猫形生物施行了一系列复杂的仪式来拯救她族中的亲属。在故事最后一幕，她复活了她的“另一位祖母”——鼹鼠。

items.name: Rapt in the King
items.description: Detailed accounts of secret bacchanals and ecstatic dances observed in necropolises and graveyards in Southern Europe, in Egypt and in Anatolia. The author is a self-confessed ghoul, an eater of buried flesh: he claims to have witnessed the dances while at his feasting.
items.description_cn: 本书详细记录了作者在南欧、埃及和安纳托利亚的坟场与墓地中看到的秘密欢宴和迷醉之舞。作者其人坦白了自己是食尸鬼，啃食土中尸体的生物：他称自己在大快朵颐时见到了书中的舞蹈。

readings.intro: The dances draw from the traditions of the Mysteries, of the cults of Isis and of Cybele, but include both symbolic and literal flayings, and the human heart is always central in the rites. The author punctuates his accounts with queasily sensuous descriptions of his own interrupted feasts.
readings.content: 'At these greater Feasts a Black Pig is always crowned as King before its Slaying. On this Occasion, its Heart was weighed in the Balance against a Knot of Feathers, and its Skin became a Cape for the Officiant. Its Flesh was left for the Crows, but I must confess my Interest was not in its Carcass but in the Perfumed Flesh of the Milliner laid fresh in the Earth.'

readings_cn.intro: 这套舞蹈源自祭奉女神伊西斯与库柏勒的密教所传承的奥秘，不仅含有象征和实际意义上的剥皮行为，而且永远以人类心脏为仪式的主轴。作者着重圈点了他对自己被打断的宴席的令人作呕的感官描写。
readings_cn.content: “在那些盛大宴席期间，总有一头黑猪在经受屠宰前被加冕为王。每逢此时，它的心脏会经天平与一片羽毛互较轻重，而它的皮会成为主祭的披风。它的血肉被留给乌鸦，但我必须坦白我意不在其尸骸，而在于女帽制造者新入土的喷了香水的肉体。”

items.name: The Viennese Conundra
items.description: Van Driel describes odd events in Vienna - the disappearance of children; epidemics of parasite activity; animal mutilations; nightmares of worms; the activities of a charitable organisation, the New Ligeians, that funds the burial of the poor. She proposes peculiar connections between these activities.
items.description_cn: 梵·德里尔描述了维也纳发生的怪事——儿童消失、寄生虫大肆传染、动物被切掉肢体、关于蠕虫的噩梦、一个为穷人提供丧葬费，名为“新生丽姬亚”的慈善组织。她指出了这些现象间怪异的联系。

readings.intro: 'When the individual K. attends the meetings, black dogs are sacrificed and quartered. When the element M. is in attendance, black mares are found with their throats slashed. I propose that these sacrifices are not necessary, but that our Ligeian friends may consider them 'fitting'. Herewith diagrams of the mutilations -'
readings.content: 'Medusa's Riddle, then, I choose to render as 'What is Not Seen?' There is another riddle, one I have heard rendered as 'What may be Lost?' I will delineate some historic attempts to answer it- these are in themselves, in some sense, sacrifices - '

readings_cn.intro: “K氏参加会议时，黑犬们被献祭并分为四块。M氏出席时，黑牝马们遭到割喉。我的意见是这些献祭是不必要的，但我们的丽姬亚朋友或许认为它们是‘恰当的’。下图是肢解的示意图——”
readings_cn.content: “那就说美杜莎的谜语吧，我选择译成‘何物不得见？’还有一道谜语，我听到的译文是‘何物会失去？’要回答此问，我会复述一些历史上著名上的作答——这些作答本身，某种意义上也是，祭品——”

items.name: Collected Hush House Lectures
items.description: In the 1800s, Dr Arun Peel was invited to give a series of lectures to the Curia. They combine his pithy view of the Histories with his particular brand of unhelpfully ironical insight.
items.description_cn: 19世纪，阿伦·褪皮博士曾应邀为决议会举办一系列的讲座。这些讲座结合了他对诸史鞭辟入里的见解与鲜明的个人标志——毫无意义的辛辣讽刺。

readings.intro: '1776, the Third History: Louis declares the Masque of Masques, and forbids mention of the Great Writhing within the walls of the Palace of Versailles, although by this point the Worms are observed to move openly along the boulevards of Paris, sometimes even in daylight. The Army is redeployed to defend the Court. The Masque lasts one lunar month, and attracts several of the Long abroad in Western Europe at the time - fleeing the Worms, or hoping to take advantage of the desperate Louis, or seeking access to the sealed mirrors of the Palace - or just eager to attend the most inventive and desperate debauch of the century…'
readings.content: 'Many Know espouse Wormish sympathies. Let a hundred Histories flourish! Tear down the tyranny of eternity! To grow Long is, usually, to cast off these sympathies. There would be no immortality without Eternity, and Eternity, we often seem to decide, is only tyranny as long as we are not eternal.'

readings_cn.intro: “1776年，第三史：路易十六宣办了假面赝会，并禁止在凡尔赛宫的宫墙内提及大蠕动，即便此时人们已经目击到蠕虫们在巴黎大街上堂而皇之地活动，有时甚至在白日之下。军队被调派去保卫王宫。假面舞会持续了整个朔望月，吸引了此时西欧各国数位长生者参加——躲避蠕虫的，或是想利用绝望的路易的，或是寻觅王宫中被封存起来的镜子的——又或者仅仅只是渴望这场这个世纪最独出心裁而绝望放荡的盛会的……”
readings_cn.content: “许多通晓者同情蠕虫。让百重历史再度繁荣！打倒永恒的暴政！而成为长生者，往往就意味着抛弃这种同情。没有永恒就没有不朽，而我们似乎总认为，只要我们未达永恒，永恒便只是暴政。”

items.name: The Debate of Seven Cups
items.description: 'Distillations of Spirit' recorded by an alchemist who identifies himself in the foreword as 'But Sir Thomas Browne's Reflexion.'
items.description_cn: 又称“灵魂的蒸馏”，由某位炼金术士记下，其在前言中自述为“仅是托马斯·布朗爵士的倒影”。

readings.intro: 'Time is a pure Flame, and we live by an invisible Sun within us.'
readings.content: 'Darkness and Light divide the Course of Time, and until that Course is Run, Eternity remains History's Bed-Fellow. Sorrow then is Sense's final Solvent, and even a Tear, should it fall enow, might destroy a Stone…'

readings_cn.content: “黑暗与光明划分了时间的历程，然而只要这一历程仍在运转，永恒就依旧是历史的枕边人。悲恸是感官的最后溶剂，即使只是眼泪，只要滴落得足够多，也或可摧毁顽石……”
readings_cn.intro: “时间是一束纯净的火焰，我们的内心都拥有一颗无形的太阳。”

items.name: The Temptations of Architecture
items.description: The antiquarian and nyctodromist Ambrose Westcott writes of the 'dangers of doors', with particular reference to a house in the bounds named 'Treowen'.
items.description_cn: 夜游术学者兼古董学家安布罗斯·威斯考特在本文中警告了“门扉的危险”，尤其着重提到了位于边境的一栋名叫“特罗文”的房子。

readings.intro: No doubt they have come to regret the ambitions of their Winding Stair; even now in Treowen, a silver sea is unwisely visible from a rash window…'
readings.content: Westcott explains that the Wheelocks, the 'charge-holders of Treowen', have had recourse to dramatic measures to prevent oneiric encroachment, removing the entire top floor of the building. 'Nevertheless,' he writes, 'the business of the Moon-Hall has begun to touch the other business of the house...'

readings_cn.content: 威斯考特解释说，作为“特罗文的管理人”，惠洛克家族不得不采取一系列夸张的措施来阻止梦境侵蚀，以至于拆除了整个房屋的顶楼。“尽管如此，”他补充道，“月厅已经开始对房屋内的其他事物施以影响……”
readings_cn.intro: “毫无疑问，他们已经开始为建造盘旋楼梯的雄心壮志而后悔；直到现今，如果有人在特罗文鲁莽地打开一扇窗，依然能不明智地看到那银色的海洋……”

items.name: The Tripled Heart
items.description: Sacred poems composed in honour of the Hours venerated by the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot.
items.description_cn: 歌颂三重绳结姐妹会所崇敬诸司辰的圣诗集。

readings.intro: The Grail is celebrated for her colours, the Malachite for her sweetness, the Axe for her constancy…
readings.content: The Thunderskin, least of the Hours of the Knot when he is even counted among their number at all, is celebrated with an unexpectedly poignant elegy. 'What lives, departs; what is dead, remains.'

readings_cn.intro: 赞颂赤杯，为她的颜色；赞颂石绿，因她的甘美；赞颂双角斧，以她的恒久……
readings_cn.content: 轰雷之皮，那位即使位列绳结诸司辰，也只占末席的神祗，被颂以一首出人意料的凄美哀歌：“生者往矣，逝者长存。”

items.name: The Five Letters On Memory
items.description: Julian Coseley's epistolary treatise on 'matters memorial and mnemonic', addressed to his then-friend Claude Hersault, the mystic and antiquarian.
items.description_cn: 朱利安·科赛利以“记忆与助记法”为主题的书信体专著，收信人是他当时的好友，神秘主义者兼古董商人，克劳德·海索。

readings.intro: The book is partly a practical manual, expounding memory-palace-like techniques, and partly an exploration of 'Memory Rarefied' - modes in which sense or experience persist outside a mortal mind.
readings.content: This is an early work, and by Coseley's standards it brims with optimism, even enthusiasm. If books, he suggests, are the memory that does not die, then 'perhaps with sufficient Endeavours, Memory's Murderer might be Contain'd'.

readings_cn.intro: 本书的一部分是本实用手册，介绍了类似“记忆宫殿”法的技巧，剩下部分则是对“稀释的记忆”的探讨——感觉或经验在凡人的头脑之外持续存在的状态。
readings_cn.content: 本书是科赛利的早期著作，按照作者本人的标准，充满了乐观、甚至是热忱。他认为，如果书籍是不死的记忆，那么“只要付出足够的努力，记忆的杀手兴许就能被牵制”。

items.name: The Twelve Letters On Consequence
items.description: Julian Coseley's epistolary treatise on 'what may come after', addressed to his once-friend Claude Hersault, the mystic and antiquarian.
items.description_cn: 朱利安·科赛利以“之后会发生什么”为主题的书信体专著，收信人是他曾经的好友，神秘主义者兼古董商人，克劳德·海索。

readings.intro: By the time he wrote these letters, Coseley was identified with the oneiropolitical 'Worms' movement, and Hersault with the 'Birds' - meaning roughly that Hersault held the order of the Hours to be desirable, and Coseley held it to be oppressive.
readings.content: Many of Coseley's arguments about consequence and finality are couched in erudite and practical alchemical terms. Others appear to be thinly-veiled threats directed at Hersault. Some are both.

readings_cn.intro: 在写下这些信笺的时候，科赛利已经被认定是梦境政治运动“蠕虫派”的支持者，而海索则是“飞鸟派”的——这大致意味着，海索认为司辰们的统治称心合意，而科赛利认为其暴虐不公。
readings_cn.content: 科赛利关于结果与终局的许多观点都是通过渊博而实用的炼金学术语来表达的。别的则是针对海索本人不加掩饰的威胁。有些则兼而有之。

items.name: Gospel of Nicodemus
items.description: An apocryphal account of the works and experiences of the Shepherd Illuminate by one of his supposed companions.
items.description_cn: 对“沐光明的牧羊人”其功业与事迹的虚构记述，由一位所谓的追随者写就。

readings.intro: 'Inventori Lucis Soli Invicto Nuntio' reads the dedication - loosely translatable as 'I am the herald of the Sun Unconquerable, Light's Contriver'. This is a variation on the more usual 'invicto augusto', the declaration which united the eastern and western traditions of the Church Solar.
readings.content: The Shepherd Illuminate, the Virgin-Born, warns of the Sun's Division but promises its ultimate reunification in the Second Dawn 'through the ministry of St Uzult'. Uzult is of course the ink of power used by Librarians of the Tree, but also venerated as a saint in some borderline heterodox solar traditions.

readings_cn.content: 沐光明的牧羊人，处女所生者，警告了太阳的分裂，但是保证它将“经由圣珀金的传道”，于第二拂晓最终重归一体。珀金当然是指唯有守夜人之树的图书管理员方能使用的一种力量之墨，但在某些边缘的异端太阳崇拜传统中，也会把其尊为圣人。
readings_cn.intro: 献词读作Inventori Lucis Soli Invicto Nuntio——大致可以译为“我是无敌太阳的使者，光明的创造者”。这段话更常见的变体是invicto augusto，而正是该宣言统一了太阳教会的东西方传统。

items.name: An Almanac of Entrances
items.description: A handbook of sealed and unsealed byways and shortcuts through the Bounds, compiled by Willem Harries in the 1860s - during his term as Librarian of Hush House.
items.description_cn: 记载了可用来穿越边境的，封闭和尚未封闭的支路和捷径的手册，由威廉·哈里斯在19世纪60年代编写——在他担任噤声居屋图书管理员的期间。

readings.intro: Harries discusses the role played by the 'Légion du Seuil' and the 'Company of the Wolf-in-Gold' in warding the Bounds against outside influences. He warns that Bounds-travellers may themselves be considered 'outside influences…'
readings.content: 'The Mansus, as Ys, lacks walls; Ys and the Mansus have both their gates, and there may be no gate without a wall. Thus the paradox resolves, as all those who walk in dream will learn. But the Wood has neither gate nor wall, and so it is the Wood whose roots may creep after us into the hours of our waking.'

readings_cn.content: “和伊苏一样，漫宿并无围墙；伊苏与漫宿都有大门，但没有围墙就没有大门。如此悖论便得到了解释，正如每个行于梦中者都会学到的那样。但是林地既无大门，也无围墙，所以其根须或会跟随我们蔓爬到醒时的时辰。”
readings_cn.intro: 哈里斯讨论了“门关军团”与“金狼兵团”在保护边境不受外界影响中担任的角色。他警告说，试图穿越边境的人本身可能便会被视为某种“外界影响”……

items.name: Just Verse
items.description: A rare surviving copy of Christopher Illopoly's notoriously unsuccessful volume of experimental poetry, published in 1912.
items.description_cn: 一本出了名失败的实验性诗集的罕见抄本，克里斯托弗·伊利奥波里著，1912年出版。

readings.intro: Illopoly is clearly more interested in the occult than the aesthetic aspects of the work. By most measures, the rhymes are contrived; the meter inconsistent; the imagery banal. Still, even the worst verses have a compelling quality, and I find myself drumming my fingers on the desk to accompany their rhythms.
readings.content: In an afterword, Illopoly discusses 'mnemonic holometaboly', by which he seems to mean a sort of crafting process where memories, when fed into a Preliminal Meter technique in the presence of enough Knock or Rose, can 'blossom and fissure' into more potent versions of themselves...

readings_cn.intro: 伊利奥波里显然更加注重这些诗的神秘学意义，而非作品本身的美学价值。照一般的衡量标准来看，它们的押韵做作；格律矛盾；意象平庸。不过，再糟糕的诗句也有其引人入胜之处，就像我发现自己的手指正在桌上合着它的韵律敲点。
readings_cn.content: 在跋文中，伊利奥波里讨论了所谓的“记忆的完全变态”。他认为这是某种制造工艺。将记忆与足够的启相或引相投入到“阈前韵律”之技术时，它们就能“盛开和绽裂”，成为它们自身某种更加强力的变体……

items.name: The Book of Cinders
items.description: Ostensibly an eighteenth-century fireworks manual, but with some exotic ingredient choices and a substantial section on 'teframancy', divination from ashes.
items.description_cn: 表面上只是本十八世纪的烟火手册，但其中有些材料的选择相当异质，还有相当一部分是关于用灰烬预言的“烬占”技术。

readings.intro: The text takes as its theme the motto of the Society of the Noble Endeavour, ALITUR PROPRIIS IGNIS CINERIBUS - 'a fire by its own ashes is nourished', and uses this as a way into discussions of alchemical techniques…
readings.content: A surprisingly casual final section mentions that iotic essence, 'the root of the Great and Exultant Ink Orpimental', can be refined with enough Forge from a variety of liquids.

readings_cn.content: 本书的最后一章出人意料而轻描淡写地提到了赤化精华——“伟大而欢欣的雌黄墨水之基底”——能在足够的铸下从各类液体中提炼。
readings_cn.intro: 本书主要以高贵之举社团的格言“ALITUR PROPRIIS IGNIS CINERIBUS”（“火焰受其灰烬滋养”）为主题，并借此讨论了炼金术的技术……

items.name: Codex Acephali
items.description: Sometimes called 'The Book of the Clean Skull'. The book contains accounts of enlightenments available through the gradual, surgical removal of the lobes of the brain.
items.description_cn: 有时也被称为“净颅之书”。本书描述了在逐步切除额叶的手术中能够获得的启示。

readings.intro: It becomes clear that the processes described are mostly allegorical or metaphorical descriptions of Winter techniques for less revolting occult work. Even the metaphors are pretty horrible, though.
readings.content: The author explains adaptations of these techniques, with sufficient Winter aspect, to harvest a mysterious substance described as the 'rags of the final bone' from the remains of almost any animal…

readings_cn.intro: 很明显，书中描写的手术过程大多是对一些冬之技术——用于不太招人反感的神秘学实践的那些——的寓言或隐喻。然而哪怕只是隐喻都骇人听闻。
readings_cn.content: 作者在文中阐明，用这些技术的变体，配合足够的冬相，便可以从几乎任何动物的遗骸中收获一种神秘物质，他称之为“最终骸骨的残余”……

items.name: The History of Inks
items.description: A legendary grimoire of exotic ink-making lore. The cover and some of the pages, unfortunately are stained and crusted with something more like mucus than ink.
items.description_cn: 一本著名的魔法书，记载了异质的墨水制作秘传。不幸的是，它的封面及一些书页，被比起墨水更像粘液的东西给弄脏结垢了。

readings.intro: 'The encaustum Marakat is refined from the liquor named leathy in the presence of Nectar aspect. The Priestesses of the Knot have also learnt to brew Marakat in this wise - yet for the nature of their arts, their task may be easier…'
readings.content: The History concludes with the admission that the encaustum named 'Orpiment Exultant' was once drawn from the veins of Forge-long. Thankfully, it seems, it can also be refined from Iotic Essence using the techniques in this book - or with 'transformations' and 'the jewel-science'.

readings_cn.intro: “名为石翠的终刻墨能在足够的蜜相下从名为遗忘之水的液体中提炼。绳结姐妹会的女祭司们也曾学会用这种方式制取石翠——考虑到她们所使用技艺的性质，她们的工艺甚至可能更简单……”
readings_cn.content: 本书在结尾处承认，名为“欢欣雌黄”的终刻墨曾是从铸之长生者的血管中提取的。值得庆幸的是，似乎也可以用本书中的技术——或者“嬗变诸法”和“宝石科学”，将它从赤化精华中提炼出来。

items.name: In the Malleary
items.description: A lively account of the creation of each jewel at the world's beginning.
items.description_cn: 本书生动地描述了每种宝石在世界伊始是如何被创造的。

readings.intro: Lively, yes; but also almost entirely nonsense. 'Pearl, the tears of the forgotten moon, caught by the Lionsmith in his net. Ruby, the blood of the first bird, stung by the Lionsmith's hammer.'
readings.content: The author is either terribly misinformed of the nature of the Hours, or - one begins to suspect - intentionally throwing up a smoke-screen to confuse seekers of the Invisible Arts. But there are some useful crumbs of fact to be picked out of the daft and gaping cracks.

readings_cn.content: 本书的作者要么严重地误解了这些司辰的本质，要么——让人不由得怀疑——是故意抛出了这些烟雾弹，来迷惑那些无形之术的寻求者。但从这些可笑和疏漏的破绽中依旧能挑选出些许有用的真相碎片。
readings_cn.intro: 本书诚然生动形象；但也几乎全是无稽之谈。“珍珠，遗忘之月的眼泪，被狮子匠的罗网捕获。红宝石，最初之鸟的鲜血，被狮子匠的铁锤刺戳。”

items.name: The Kerisham Portolan
items.description: A beautifully illustrated and heavily annotated 'portolan' - a nautical atlas of ports and destinations.
items.description_cn: 一本附有精美插图和大量注释的“波特兰图”——标注港口与目的地的海上地图集。

readings.intro: It quickly becomes clear that many of its destinations no longer exist, or never existed in the traditional sense, but the annotations remain fascinating. The routes to Noon, the Long-sanctuary across the Western Sea, may remain viable…
readings.content: Two pages have been gummed together. When teased apart they reveal a route to 'Ys Behind the Wave' - marked in red and gold inks with heavily underlined warnings. 'HERE THE FINAL CITY'. 'STRIKE THE HOURS.' 'LEST EARTH AND SKY BREAK OPEN…'

readings_cn.intro: 很快就能发现，书中的很多目的地已然不复存在，或是在传统意义上就不曾存在过，但对它们的注释依然令人着迷。通往西海彼岸的长生者庇护所，也就是午港的航线，也许依然可以使用……
readings_cn.content: 有两张书页被粘在一起。将它们仔细分开后，露出了一条通往“波涛外的伊苏”的航线——以红色与金色的墨水标记，一旁写有带粗下划线的警告。“此为最终之城”“撼动司辰”“唯恐天崩地裂”……

items.name: Nix Abolix
items.description: A grim treatise on 'those feasts that occur, those feasts that are not to be witnessed.'
items.description_cn: 一篇关于“那些发生的盛宴，那些不可见证的盛宴”的严肃论文。

readings.intro: The alukites, who feasted on their children and became monsters. The dragon-kinds among the Carapace Cross, who feasted on Hour-flesh and became monsters. The khalvites, who drank of Echidna's bounty, and became monsters…
readings.content: 'Marinette, the Ligeian: so young, so hungry. All her children cannot slake her thirst. When Moth rose, another held the Flaying Key, but at the Grail's bidding did Marinette consume that she.'

readings_cn.intro: 阿卢卡因吞食自己的子嗣而变成怪物。介壳种中的龙族因啖噬司辰的遗骸而变成怪物。餮猊因饮下厄客德娜的馈赠而变成怪物……
readings_cn.content: “丽姬亚玛丽内特：如此年轻，如此饥饿。她所有的子嗣都无法抚平她的干渴。当飞蛾升起之时，剥皮之钥曾为另一人所持有，但在圣杯的命令下，玛丽内特将她吞食殆尽。”

items.name: OGHKOR OGHKOR TISSILAK OGHKOR
items.name_cn: 《奥格科尔 奥格科尔 蒂西拉克 奥格科尔》
items.description: A surprisingly chatty text by an entity that identifies itself as 'the Excellency Gnathobasis'.
items.description_cn: 一篇令人啧啧称奇的对话体文本，由一位自称“巨颚阁下”的存在写下。

readings.intro: The Excellency Gnathobasis explains the 'limbs and extensions' of potent and dangerous 'glyphic achievements'. The sentences are nonsense on first reading, but quickly acquire an insistent meaning on each repetition.
readings.content: 'With adequate Grail,' the Excellency Gnathobasis explains, 'the Pale Mommet wakes to life. With generous Grail, the Flushed Mommet accepts our beneficence. It may be necessary to overcome scruple! The Excellency Gnathobasis will assure you as to how, and to whom, and with which most perfect instrument.'

readings_cn.content: “提供足够的杯，”巨颚阁下提到，“就能唤醒苍白人偶。提供大量的杯，靥红人偶就会接受我们的馈赠。克服顾虑可能是必要的！巨颚阁下将告诉你，如何，由谁，及用哪种最完美的小工具能做到这些。”
readings_cn.intro: 巨颚阁下讲解了某种强力而危险的“象形文字”的“分支与延伸”。这些句子在初读时似乎没有任何意义，但只要重读几遍，就能很快理解其中的含义。

results.result_name: Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars

items.name: The Radical Measure
items.description: Manifesto for experimental and dangerous-sounding invocatory poetry, written some time in the nineteenth century by Dr Arun Peel. A notoriously inconsistent and incoherent text, apparently produced in a tearing hurry.
items.description_cn: 本宣言由阿伦·褪皮博士发表于十九世纪，为实验性与危言耸听的祈祷诗所作。其行文出了名地前后矛盾而语无伦次，显然是在仓促之间写下的。

readings.intro: 'The Hours have little time for poetry,' Dr Peel avers, 'but they have a tremendous amount of time for poets.'
readings.content: 'As the Rose opens,' Dr Peel explains, 'an Enduring memory opens to the Horizon. This is a way of saying something that cannot otherwise be said, and is best only written with one's eyes firmly closed.'

readings_cn.intro: “司辰极少有时间作诗，”褪皮博士断言道，“但祂们有许多的时间给诗人。”
readings_cn.content: “随着罗盘玫瑰的盛放，”褪皮博士解释说，“某种弥久持续的回忆也会随之在地平线开放。这是一种表达无法用其他方式表达之事的方法，而记录它的最好方法唯有闭紧双眼。”

items.name: The Radical Measure (Glossed)
items.description: The original 'Radical Measures' was a manifesto for experimental poetry with occult properties, written in the nineteenth century by Dr Arun Peel. The original is notoriously incoherent - much later, Christopher Illopoly took on the task of editing and glossing it. He has taken some liberties, but the updated version is generally well regarded.
items.description_cn: 初版的《激进举措》发表于十九世纪，是一部关于神秘学创新实验性诗歌的宣言，作者为阿伦·褪皮博士。原著是出了名地语无伦次——直到很久之后，克里斯托弗·伊利奥波里接受了修订与润色这篇宣言的工作。他做了一些大胆的改动，但改动后的版本受到了一致好评。

readings.intro: 'The Hours have little time for poetry,' Dr Peel avers, 'but they have a tremendous amount of time for poets.' (Illopoly has added a note suggesting this should in fact be 'the most tremendous time with poets'.)
readings.content: 'As the Rose opens,' Dr Peel explains, 'Enduring Memory opens to the Horizon. This is a way of saying something that cannot otherwise be said, and is best only written with one's eyes firmly closed.' (Illopoly's gloss reads: Horizon-Sight synthesis method. Reverse procedure, with Knock, to elaborate Gervinite in the Chronsichord mode.)

readings_cn.intro: “司辰极少有时间作诗，”褪皮博士断言道，“但祂们有许多的时间给诗人。”（伊利奥波里补充道，这意味着事实上“祂们和诗人共度了最漫长的时光”。）
readings_cn.content: “随着罗盘玫瑰的盛放，”褪皮博士解释说，“某种弥久持续的回忆也会随之在地平线开放。这是一种表达无法用其他方式表达之事的方法，而记录它的最好方法唯有闭紧双眼。”（伊利奥波里的脚注：极目远眺的合成法。改用启，以相反的步骤则能激活格维合金，使之进入时键琴模式。）

items.name: Book of Miah
items.description: An account of the 'five visits of the Desert Wanderer' - probably the Hour called the Vagabond - to the city Miah. She begins as a delighted child - perhaps even a mortal - but things then go badly…
items.description_cn: 记述了“沙漠漫游者的五次造访”——可能是被称为浪游旅人的那位司辰对弥阿城的造访。她最开始是个快乐的孩子——可能甚至只是个凡人——但之后事态愈发糟糕……

readings.intro: 'In her second visit, she came as Laughingthrush. Her heart was bright within, her beak was ripe with song, but in the first moment her feathers touched the city stones, the laughter began….'
readings.content: The Wanderer's penultimate visit is as Centipede, whose 'venom cracks stone'. Miah is abandoned to the desert. But she returns one last time, again as Laughingthrush, with four other Hours who take the shape of birds, 'to celebrate the First Roost above the bones of her hated kin.'

readings_cn.intro: “第二次造访时，她化为笑鸫。她的内心轻松愉悦，她的喙中饱含欢歌。但在她的羽毛碰触到城市的岩石的那一刻，那笑声便开始……”
readings_cn.content: 在倒数第二次造访时，漫游者化为蜈蚣，她的毒液“让岩石开裂”。弥阿被弃于沙漠。而她最后一次归来时，再次化为笑鸫，与同样变成鸟形的另外四位司辰一起，“在她可憎亲族的白骨上庆贺第一栖木的建立。”

items.name: The Intimations of Skin
items.description: Fiendishly complex, weirdly distorted illustrations of 'congress and anatomy' by the haunted visionary painter Niels Frederik Malskær.
items.description_cn: 鬼魅繁复、扭曲变形的插画集，以“交媾与解剖”为主题，由痛苦不安的灵视画家尼尔斯·弗雷德里克·马斯凯尔创作。

readings.intro: Malskær illuminates the evolutions of the Names of the Grail with unfortunate clarity. It seems that a Lovely who consumes an Ivory becomes an Ivory. A Lovely who consumes a Thirstly becomes a Thirstly. A Lovely who consumes a Name of another Hour might take its place...
readings.content: In the penultimate illustration, a Lovely grapples with a fungoid knot that can only be a Name of the Crowned Growth. The Lovely's mouth and other portals gape wide, and the Growth-Name is already partially engulfed - but it seems that Malskær couldn't bring himself to illustrate the result, and the final illustration is only a scrawled, bloated obscurity.

readings_cn.intro: 马斯凯尔阐明了圣杯的具名者的嬗变，清晰程度却不甚令人满意。吞噬骨白者的美貌者会变成骨白者，吞噬干渴者的美貌者会变成干渴者。吞噬其他司辰具名者的美貌者可能会取而代之……
readings_cn.content: 在倒数第二幅插画中，一位美貌者与一个真菌结团缠斗在一起，后者只能是戴冠之孳的具名者。美貌者的嘴巴和其他门户大张，而戴冠之孳的具名者已经部分被吞噬一一但马斯凯尔似乎无法为这一结果绘图，最终的作品只是一团潦草而臃肿的晦涩。

items.name: The Berrybook
items.description: Thirza Blake, seventh librarian of Hush House, talks about fruit. For no other apparent reason but that it was the kind of thing she did, she talks about fruit in the woven language Killasimi.
items.description_cn: 蒂尔扎·布雷克，噤声居屋的第七任图书管理员，在本书中讨论了果实的秘密。本书以“织就之语”夜魄语写就，没有其他特殊理由，只是因为她这人就是会这么做。

readings.intro: 'Who was it once said, fruit is the womb of a plant? It was me. Take a few moments to think on that enripened wisdom. I shall leave a blank space for your moments, here in this page.'
readings.content: 'Nectar, children mine - cast my words into a sufficiency of Nectar and watch the pyrus pyrissimus burst from wood. Gather more Nectar! Wring it from the trees and earth! And our pyrissimus gushes forth the Sacrament! You will thank me.'

readings_cn.intro: “是谁曾说过，果实是植物之子宫？是我。花些时间思考这丰富多汁的智慧吧。我会留些空白供你们思考，就是这页。”
readings_cn.content: “花蜜，我的孩子们——将我的话语浸入充足的蜜中，然后你就能看着枯木上绽裂出铜梨。收集更多的蜜！从树木与大地中将它们榨取出来！你会看到汁水从圣餐中不断涌出！你会为此而感谢我的。”

items.name: Seven Shards
items.description: The Lionsmith, one of the two great Hours of struggle, broke his sword into seven shards. Natalia Brulleau, fifth Librarian of Hush House, describes the nature of each of those shards, allegorically and otherwise.
items.description_cn: 作为司掌斗争的两位伟大司辰之一，狮子匠曾将他的佩剑碎为七片。噤声居屋的第五任图书管理员，纳塔莉娅·布鲁洛夫以寓言及其他形式描述了每一块碎片的特性。

readings.intro: 'The Third Shard then has been identified with 'the cry of pain'. The Lionsmith is a stoic Hour, but we must assume that in the Sundering Moment even he might have been unable to restrain his distress. Now the sound of tin under pressure we call the 'tin cry' - a reason, perhaps, for the further identification of the Third Shard as the 'Shard Royal'...
readings.content: 'The Seventh Shard we call, informally, the Invincible Audacity, which is struck from the Winning Move as the Winning Move is struck from a memory - with the application of sufficient Edge.'

readings_cn.intro: “于是第三碎片被定义为‘痛苦悲鸣’。狮子匠是位坚忍的司辰，但我们不得不推测，即便是他也无法在分离之刻抑制自己的痛苦。如今我们把锡在重压下发出的声音称之为‘锡鸣’——恐怕这就是把第三碎片进一步命名为‘王者碎片’的原因……”
readings_cn.content: “我们将第七碎片非正式地称作无敌勇莽，它能从致胜之着中崩出，如同致胜之着从回忆中崩出——只要运用足够的刃。”

items.name: The Crossing to Noon
items.description: The mystic Garcia Sauri gives a picaresque account of the adventures of Franklin Bancroft, 'Prince of Wines', and Eva Dewulf, 'the Pale Lady', on their way to the hidden island of Noon.
items.description_cn: 神秘主义者加西亚·绍里用一种浪荡汉冒险小说式的口吻，讲述了“葡萄酒王子”富兰克林·班克罗夫特与“苍白女士”伊娃·德沃尔夫前往隐秘午岛的冒险。

readings.intro: 'For a long long time the Blackbone pondered her next move, until the Moon dared to peep from behind a cloud, and the Prince completed the composition of his third sestina. But the Lady met the blind gaze of its open pores, waiting for the tide…'
readings.content: Garcia Sauri acknowledges in an epilogue that it is widely known that Eva in fact tragically drowned herself - and her twin infant grand-daughters - without ever making such a journey. But he adds contemptuously: 'it is also widely known that the City Unbuilt will so remain, that only one History is ever written, and that Janus is a Mansus-prank.'

readings_cn.intro: “在这漫长的时间里，黑骸思索着她的下一步行动……直到月亮敢于从云缝间窥视，王子则趁机构思好了今晚的第三首六节诗。女士却对上了它那张开孔隙的盲目凝视，等待浪潮……”
readings_cn.content: 众所周知，伊娃最终悲惨地自溺身亡——与她尚年幼的双胞胎孙女一起——从未踏上旅途。加西亚·绍里在结语中承认这点，但又轻蔑地补充道：“同样众所周知的是，未建之城将保持未建；只有一重历史是书就的；雅努斯只是漫宿的恶作剧。”

items.name: What Does Not Bark
items.description: Alexander Probst writes warily of 'Calyptra' - a law, principle or society which prevents the dissemination of dangerous knowledge.
items.description_cn: 亚历山大·普罗布斯特在本书中小心翼翼地提到了“根冠”——一种阻止危险知识传播的法则、准则或是组织。

readings.intro: 'Calyptra, like the planet that occludes the star, or the Doylian dog that fails to bark, can be identified only by its absence. Even the name, I think, must be a mask…'
readings.content: 'Calyptra is said to make exceptions specifically for the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. Does it make those exceptions so the Hours can make use of them?'

readings_cn.intro: “根冠，就如同遮蔽了恒星的行星，如同柯南·道尔那不曾吠叫的看门犬，仅能靠其缺失来识别。就连这名字，想必也只是面具……”
readings_cn.content: “据说根冠会为守夜人之树的图书馆破例。根冠留下种种例外，是为了让诸司辰得以利用它们吗？”

items.name: Stolen Histories
items.description: The agitator and pamphleteer Alexander Sparrow inveighs against the 'monstrous Serpents, Thieves of History.'
items.description_cn: 煽动者与宣传册作者亚历山大·斯派鹭在本文中强烈抨击了“可怕的巨蛇，历史的窃贼”。

readings.intro: Sparrow acknowledges five Histories, insists the Third History may be 'overrun by Coils', warns the Fifth History is already lost.
readings.content: Sparrow, with his usual paranoia, appears to be conflating the horror of the Worm Wars and the Great Writhing with the activities of the Great Hooded Princes. Still, he draws thought-provoking comparisons between the Princes - normally conceived as exotic Knock-long - and the widely feared Worms.

readings_cn.intro: 斯派鹭承认有五重历史，并坚称第三史可能“蟠蛇泛滥成灾”，并警告称第五史已然失落。
readings_cn.content: 斯派鹭，带着他一贯的偏执，似乎把蠕虫大战和大蠕动的恐怖，与兜颈贵胄们的活动混为一谈。尽管如此，他在贵胄与广受恐惧的蠕虫之间所做的比较依然引人深思，前者通常被认为是一类来自异乡的启之长生者。

items.name: Black Nephrite
items.description: One of Valentine Dewulf's dream-journals, in which he records his visions of 'a place that is no place, beneath the house that is no house.'
items.description_cn: 瓦伦丁·德沃尔夫的梦境日记之一，记录了他曾见到过的，关于某个“在非居屋之居屋下的非空间之空间”的幻象。

readings.intro: The dark, inchoate, feral space described by Valentine seems to be the 'Nowhere' of the Invisible Arts - the infra-oneiric lair of the alien Hours sometimes called gods-from-Nowhere.
readings.content: Valentine's attitude to the Nowhere-Hours is unexpectedly relaxed. He speaks darkly of their appetites, but he insists they are too alien to penetrate the House of the Sun, let alone the waking world. He even seems to suggest that the Mansus-Hours have exaggerated the threat of the Nowhere-Hours for their own reasons. 'Not all Birds are trustworthy in their Feathers', he warns.

readings_cn.intro: 瓦伦丁所描述的黑暗、蛮荒、阴郁的空间，似乎就是无形之术中的“虚界”——梦境之下的世界，是有时被称为虚源神的异类司辰的巢穴。
readings_cn.content: 瓦伦丁对虚界司辰的态度意外地平和。他阴暗地提到了祂们的胃口，但又坚持认为祂们太过异类，无法入侵太阳的居屋，更不消说醒时世界。他甚至似乎认为，漫宿司辰出于自身的原因夸大了虚源神的威胁。他警告称：“并非所有飞鸟的羽翎都值得信赖。”

items.name: The Sea Does Not Regret
items.description: Ehsan Fekri, one-time Secretary Salvant of the Curia of the Isle - responsible for the Curia's healing efforts - writes of his experiences in Brancrug, and hints at his travels elsewhere.
items.description_cn: 埃桑·费克里曾任岛屿决议会的护理理事，负责决议会的治疗事务。他记录了在布兰库格的经历，并暗示了他在其他地方旅行时的见闻。

readings.intro: 'The Sea does not regret the tide,' Fekri writes, 'for when the tide has passed, it leaves its traces on the sand; which traces are the Sea's memory.'
readings.content: Fekri is a keen fisherman, and speaks glowingly of the fish suppers of Brancrug. He also admits that his enthusiasm for 'the bounty of the sea' has altered him - that before he came to Brancrug, he consumed only those things found in the earth. 'I was the greater thereby, but all of us give up what we were, to become what we are.'

readings_cn.intro: “大海从不后悔潮水涨落，”费克里写道，“因为当潮水退去，它会在沙滩上留下痕迹；这痕迹便是大海的记忆。”
readings_cn.content: 费克里热衷于钓鱼，他在书中也兴致高涨地谈到了布兰库格对鱼的各种烹饪方式。他也承认，对“大海的馈赠”的热忱转变了他——在来到布兰库格之前，他只吃从大地中找到的东西。“故而我过去曾强大得多。但我们每个人都舍弃了曾经的自己，才变成了现在的我们。”

items.name: Two Wombs, One Heart
items.description: A fanciful account by Thirza Blake of the early life of the Twins - their time as mortals before they became Hours or even Long, in a 'dry kingdom beyond the Western Sea' which Thirza suggests might have been ancient Mexico.
items.description_cn: 蒂尔扎·布雷克对孪生子的早期经历的想象性描述，远在她们成为司辰，甚至长生者之前；那时她们还作为凡人生活在“西海彼岸的干燥王国”，蒂尔扎认为那可能就是古墨西哥。

readings.intro: 'It is widely known that the Sister was rich and the Witch poor. It is widely known that the Witch loved the Sister first. It is not widely known that the Witch was first employed to teach the Sister the arts of embroidery…'
readings.content: Although Thirza is very probably just making up much of the story, there are long passages expounding notable techniques of weave-work and thread-feit. In particular, when Witch and Sister flee across the Sea to be together, Thirza explains how they fashioned a 'peace-weave' with Heart and these arts, and then, to tame the winds, called on Heart again to swaddle the thunder in the peace-weave.

readings_cn.intro: “众所周知，巫女富有，女巫贫穷。同样众所周知的是女巫先爱上了巫女。而鲜为人知的是：女巫先受雇教授巫女刺绣的技艺……”
readings_cn.content: 尽管这些故事的大部分内容可能都是蒂尔扎杜撰的，但本书确实有相当的篇幅阐述了值得注意的、有关编织和穿线的技术。尤其是在描写女巫和巫女为了厮守而横渡大海的桥段时，蒂尔扎讲解了她们是如何通过心与这些技艺编织出“平息之网”，以及为了驯服风暴，她们如何再次唤起心，用平息之网裹住了雷霆。

items.name: One Hundred And Eight
items.description: Eva Dewulf discurses on the Fifth History, and particularly on those who are said to have 'passed over' from it - the Great Hooded Princes, the Knock-long who ascended under the Mother of Ants but now (so Eva claims) honour the Horned-Axe.
items.description_cn: 伊娃·德沃尔夫对第五史的论述，着重讨论了那些据说已经从中“抹去”者——兜颈贵胄，曾在蚁母麾下擢升，如今（伊娃如此声称）却转而侍奉双角斧的启之长生者们。

readings.intro: 'The Great Hooded Princes call their library the Tomb of Lies, and this has given rise to a foolish tradition that the Princes are habitual liars. Of course, in fact, Truth flourishes when Lies are slain. On the other hand, the Princes do not say 'Knowledge is Power', but rather, 'Power is Knowledge.'
readings.content: Eva has, to her regret, never visited the Library. She notes that it is said to be 'west of the Lion, and north of Victory' - and suggests that, although the Princes are generally associated with India, their library might be farther East…

readings_cn.intro: “兜颈贵胄把它们的图书馆称为谎言之墓，而这导致人们常愚蠢地误认为贵胄们都谎话连篇。当然，事实上，当谎言被消灭时，真实才会繁盛。另一方面，贵胄们从不说‘知识就是力量’，而是说‘力量就是知识’。”
readings_cn.content: 伊娃为自己从来没去过那座图书馆而感到遗憾。她提到，据说图书馆在“狮子以西，胜利以北”——而且认为，尽管兜颈贵胄一般都与印度有关联，但它们的图书馆大概在更遥远的东方……

items.name: The World Despoil'd
items.description: Subtitled 'the Flowers in the Waste': an epic poem that presents a medical treatise through allegory. The author is Gideon Dewulf, 5th Baron Brancrug, sometimes unkindly called 'the Cutter'.
items.description_cn: 副标题为“荒野中的花朵”：一本以寓言形式呈现医学论述的史诗。作者是第五代布兰库格男爵基甸·德沃尔夫，他有时也被刻薄地称作“切割者”。

readings.intro: The poem is a substantial variation on the Fisher-King tale. A wounded wasteland monarch learns that he and his land can be cured, but that the cure is their own response to ever more savage maladies…
readings.content: Gideon concludes with a concrete example: that the Mysteries can be used to despoil 'mine own Soaks', but then the Soak can then be refined with sufficient Heart into 'the sanguis saltandis'.

readings_cn.intro: 本书的韵诗部分基于渔夫王的传说，但进行了大量的改编。一位荒原的受伤君王得知他与他的土地可以被治愈，但疗法是将把他们引向更加野蛮的病态行径……
readings_cn.content: 基甸在最后举了个具体的应用范例：书中的奥秘可以用来掠夺“吾之浸液”，但若是唤起足够的心，就能将它进一步提炼为“舞动之血”。

items.name: An Impertinent Vitulation
items.description: A book of kitchen-garden techniques and aphrodisiac recipes recorded by Ernestine Peterhans, the 'Iron Seneschale' of Hush House for three generations of Dewulfs.
items.description_cn: 一本关于家庭菜园的园艺技术与催情食谱的书，由侍奉了三任德沃尔夫领主的噤声居屋“铁总管”，欧内斯汀·彼得汉斯记录成册。

readings.intro: Peterhans asserts casually that the rousing liquor called 'Rubywise Ruin', which Leaves & Thorns techniques can brew from flowers, was a favourite of the notoriously severe Baron Thomas. If true, this would have raised eyebrows had it been known in his lifetime...
readings.content: Peterhans mentions that one of these Leaves & Thorns techniques, with sufficient Nectar aspect, can supposedly cause 'a marvellous copper fruit' to burst from wood, although she has never managed it herself - but in a 'certain season' the pear-trees in the Practic Garden will deliver something similar.

readings_cn.intro: 彼得汉斯随口提到，用“叶片与棘刺”技术可以从花中酿造出一种激发欲望的饮品，其名为“沉沦赤慧”，是以严肃著称的托马斯男爵的爱饮。若此言不虚，并在其生前就为人所知的话，想必会让人们目瞪口呆……
readings_cn.content: 彼得汉斯也提到，用“叶片与棘刺”技术中的一种，与足够的蜜相，据信可以在枯木上绽裂出“神奇的铜皮果实”，虽然她自己从来没有做到过——但在“特定时节”，习武园的梨树上也会结出十分类似的东西。

items.name: Cardea's Delights
items.description: The third volume of Abbot Geffrey's hypothetical theological dialogues in the Socratic mode.
items.description_cn: 杰弗里院长撰写的苏格拉底式假想神学对话录，第三卷。

readings.intro: 'If Janus were an Hour, Cardea might be counted among his Names, but the world has never turned in such a manner, and so she is not…'
readings.content: Geffrey discusses the 'living Signs' - signs which change their shape, and whose flexibility is part of what makes it identifiable. He gives as one example 'the Paradox of the Hinge', and draws comparisons with the 'Names' called Twins (who would be considered Hours beyond the Church). He hints at the 'Amethyst Vessel' which can be sanctified by the Great Signs in the presence of Knock...

readings_cn.content: 杰弗里讨论了“活的符印”——可以改变自己形状的符印，其活动性本身就是其可识别性的部分原因。他以“铰链的悖论”为例，并与被称为孪生子的“具名者们”（她们在教会之外被认为是司辰）做了比较。他还暗示了“紫水晶容器”可以用伟大符印与启来加以圣化……
readings_cn.intro: “如果雅努斯是一位司辰，那么卡尔迪亚或许会被列为他的具名者，但是世界从未以这样的方式拧转，所以她不是……”

results.result_name: Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars

items.name: The Elations of Limentinus
items.description: The second volume of Abbot Geffrey's hypothetical theological debates in the Socratic mode.
items.description_cn: 杰弗里院长撰写的苏格拉底式假想神学对话录，第二卷。

readings.intro: 'If Janus were an Hour, Limentinus might be counted among his Names, but Janus has never passed that threshold, and so Limentinus is not…'
readings.content: Geffrey discusses 'the signs upon the Threshold', drawing comparisons between the duties of guest and host, and the status accorded to Hours and other powers who dwell in, are permitted in, or are forbidden access to the House of the Sun. (It was of course Geffrey who later invited censure by giving sanctuary to Natan of Regensburg, in an age when the Jews were by royal order unwelcome anywhere in the kingdom.)

readings_cn.content: 杰弗里讨论了“门关上的符印”，将宾客和主人的责任，与司辰及其他神灵中居于太阳居屋者，获准进入太阳居屋者，以及被禁入太阳居屋者之间的地位差别作了对比。（当然，杰弗里日后正是因为向雷根斯堡的纳坦提供了庇护而招致谴责。在那个年代，根据王室的规定，犹太人在王国的任何地方都不应受欢迎。）
readings_cn.intro: “如果雅努斯是一位司辰，那么利门提努斯或许会被列为他的具名者，但是雅努斯从未跨越那道门关，所以利门提努斯不是……”

results.result_name: Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars

items.name: The Raptures of Forculus
items.description: The first volume of Abbot Geffrey's hypothetical theological debates in the Socratic mode.
items.description_cn: 杰弗里院长撰写的苏格拉底式假想神学对话录，第一卷。

readings.intro: 'If Janus were an Hour, Forculus might be counted among his Names, but that door remains closed, and so Forculus is not…'
readings.content: Geffrey discusses 'the signs that mark Doors', which might permit or forbid access to certain thoughts and dreams, speculating (carefully) on which of the sanctioned Hours might teach or govern each sign.

readings_cn.content: 杰弗里讨论了“标记门关的符印”，这些符印也许能起到允许或禁止进入特定的思想与梦境的作用；并（小心翼翼地）推测了每个符印由哪些受许的司辰指引或支配。
readings_cn.intro: “如果雅努斯是一位司辰，那么福尔库鲁斯或许会被列为他的具名者，但那扇门扉仍然闭合，所以福尔库鲁斯不是……”

results.result_name: Lesson: The Great Signs and the Great Scars

items.name: Snare of the Tree: Collected Proverbs of Aunt Mopsy
items.name_cn: 《树的陷阱：莫普西阿姨的谚语集》
items.description: 'Once in the Wood, we call a visit. Twice in the Wood, we call a journey. Thrice, we call coming home.'
items.description_cn: “第一次进入林地，我们称之为拜访。第二次进入林地，我们称之为旅行。第三次，我们称之为归家。”

readings.intro: 'Every timber has its knots, the straight and the crooked both. Every weave is more absence than thread. You can't keep Nowhere out any more than you can keep Somewhere in…'
readings.content: 'When the cuckoo learns the nightingale's song, our sleep is sweeter than honey.'

readings_cn.intro: “树木不论弯直都有节疤。织物的缝隙总是多于编线。你无法将无处拒之门外，甚过把有处迎入门内……”
readings_cn.content: “当杜鹃学会了夜莺的歌声，我们的睡眠就会比蜜更香甜。”

items.name: De Ratio Quercuum
items.description: In English the title translates roughly as 'the Account of the Oaks'; but this is Nathaniel Darcy-Evers' fascinating, if haphazard, survey of the occult properties of every tree he can find, not just oaks.
items.description_cn: 标题的拉丁语大意为“橡树之理”；但实际上是纳撒尼尔·达西-埃弗斯对他所能找到的所有树木其神秘学特性的调查，而非仅仅是橡树。本书虽杂乱无章，却引人入胜。

readings.intro: 'In Persia taxus baccata, the yew, is called sorkhdar, which is 'the red tree'. There they had long understood the Grail-Root. In later times, the Great King of Pontus had bee-hives set in the branches of the oldest of the female trees….'
readings.content: 'The berries of the Pontine Yew open the door to death but the honey of their flowers opens a different door entirely. This was not the Great King's mithridate but one who has suckled at the Great Yew fears poison no longer. Perhaps they should…' Nathaniel is here distracted, however, by the toxic properties of certain inks. He does mention more usefully that the minor Ink of Power, Yewgall, can be brewed through the Rites of the Roots with the assistance of the aspect Nectar.

readings_cn.intro: “在波斯，taxus baccata，即紫杉，被称为sorkhdar，意为‘红色的树’。他们对杯之根系早有了解。再后来，本都的伟大国王在最古老的雌树的枝条上安置了蜂箱……”
readings_cn.content: “本都紫杉的浆果开启通往死亡的大门，但它的蜂蜜却能打开一扇截然不同的大门。这不是那位伟大国王的mithridate（万灵药），但饮下了伟大紫杉馈赠的人确实能够百毒不侵。也许他们应该……”但写到这里时，纳撒尼尔被某种墨水的毒性分散了注意力。他确实提到了更加有用的信息，那就是可以使用“根系之仪”，在蜜相的帮助下调制出一种次要的力量之墨，杉瘿墨。

items.name: Opus Magnum Caeruleum
items.description: Ambrose Westcott used to render the title of this venerable and anonymous work mockingly as 'the Big Blue Business'. A kinder translation would be 'the Great Work in Azure'.
items.description_cn: 这本匿名著作的标题曾被安布罗斯·威斯考特戏谑地翻译为“蓝色大把戏”。而更公允的翻译应当是“蔚蓝大功业”。

readings.intro: The reasons for Westcott's enmity to this work are clear to any pyroglyphicist: it was written at least two centuries before he was born, but anticipates or undermines many of his preferred conclusions.
readings.content: The 'Work' in question is the creation of the 'blue gold' allegedly necessary for the terrible Rite which allows a Forge-long to become a Name. The book mentions that Pyroglyphics techniques can be used with Forge to create Iotic Essence as a necessary component; but withholds the final step, insisting that the consequences are too dire, and that any interest should remain only a matter of theory.

readings_cn.content: 此述中的“功业”指的是“蓝金”的制作过程，依其叙述，在将铸之长生者擢升为具名者的可怕仪式中，这种材料是必需的。书中提到，将“焰篆体”之技术与铸一起使用，可以提炼出必要的中间产物，赤化精华；却拒绝透露最后的步骤，作者坚称这么做的后果太过可怕，因此对它的任何兴趣都只应停留在理论层面上。
readings_cn.intro: 威斯考特对这本著作抱有敌意的原因对任何焰篆学家来说都是显而易见的：本作至少在他出生两个世纪前就写成，却预见或动摇了许多他青睐的结论。

items.name: Sunrise Awakenings
items.description: An uncharacteristically poignant meditation by the Edge-long Twrog of Meirionnydd, who later came to Hush House under a variety of other names, often in search of some sort of fight.
items.description_cn: 一份犀利的非典型沉思录，作者系刃之长生者，梅里昂郡的图瓦格。他日后用许多化名拜访过噤声居屋，通常是为了寻求某种战斗。

readings.intro: 'If Light were not silent, it would be Music. If Music were visible, it would be Light…'
readings.content: Each day's light, Twrog suggests, is faintly touched by the light of every past day; so in the light of every present day, we may begin to understand something of days to come. At least, this appears to be his conclusion, but he stops in mid-sentence, apparently having lost patience with the act of writing, or possibly been ambushed.

readings_cn.content: 图瓦格认为，每天的光都被过去每天的光轻抚；所以通过当下每天的光，我们或许能够开始认识到未来会发生的事。至少，这似乎是他得出的结论，但文章却在此戛然而止，显然是他对这个主题失去了兴趣，亦或是遭受了某人的伏击。
readings_cn.intro: “若光有声，它就会变成音乐。若音乐可见，它就会变成光……”

items.name: De Horis book 1
items.description: An occasionally coherent catalogue of the secret gods, organised by hour. This is a reprint, but in the original Latin.
items.description_cn: 一套隐秘诸神的名册，这些神明被以时辰来排列组织，内容半通不通。这是重印本，但是由原著使用的拉丁语写就。

readings.intro: This volume deals mostly with the Hours of the Wood: the Moth, the Black-Flax, the Ring-Yew, among others.
readings.content: 'The Glory is a question, and the Moth always answers 'Yes'.'

readings_cn.intro: 本卷主要讲述了林地司辰中飞蛾、漆黑亚麻和环杉的故事。
readings_cn.content: “辉光是一个疑问，飞蛾总以肯定作答。”

items.name: De Horis book 2
items.description: In Latin. A nineteenth-century reprint (by the indefatigable Nathaniel Darcy-Evers) of a fourteenth-century Latin translation of a fourth-century work.
items.description_cn: 拉丁语著。一本于四世纪成书，于十四世纪被译为拉丁语的著作在十九世纪的重印版（作者为不知疲倦的纳撒尼尔·达西-埃弗斯）。

readings.intro: This volume deals mostly with the Hour called Lionsmith, the Hour called the Tribune of Scars, and with their enmity.
readings.content: 'The Lionsmith makes monsters to defeat the Tribune; but the scars of the Tribune are each a weapon.'

readings_cn.intro: 本卷主要讲述了名为狮子匠与伤疤护民官的司辰，及两者敌对的故事。
readings_cn.content: “狮子匠造出诸多怪物意图击败伤疤护民官，然而护民官身上的每一道伤疤都是武器。”

items.name: De Horis book 3
items.description: In Latin. A nineteenth-century reprint (by the indefatigable Nathaniel Darcy-Evers) of a fourteenth-century Latin translation of a fourth-century work.
items.description_cn: 拉丁语著。一本于四世纪成书，于十四世纪被译为拉丁语的著作在十九世纪的重印版（作者为不知疲倦的纳撒尼尔·达西-埃弗斯）。

readings.intro: This is usually described as the third volume of 'De Horis', but Darcy-Evers' foreword argues persuasively that it's a substantial reworking by the original author…
readings.content: The Lionsmith makes monsters, the Colonel has his scars, but the De Horis now insists that neither can truly defeat the other; that they must at some level understand these limits in their strategies; and that their enmity is an 'eternal engine of the world.'

readings_cn.intro: 这本书常被认为是《司辰志》的第三卷，但是达西-埃弗斯的前言极具说服力地认为，本书是由原作者对先前作品的实质性改编……
readings_cn.content: 狮子匠创造怪物，上校身负伤疤，而《司辰志》现在坚称，二者均不可能真正将对方击败；祂们一定在某种程度上理解自己在战略中受到的这些限制；祂们的仇怨正是“世界的永恒引擎”。

items.name: Travelling at Night, vol 1
items.description: The annotated dream-journals of Christopher Illopoly, sometimes called 'the only readable occultist': literate, entertaining, bewildering.
items.description_cn: 带注解的克里斯托弗·伊利奥波里的梦境手记，有时也被称为“唯一能读懂的密教典籍”：文笔精妙，富有趣味，扑朔迷离。

readings.intro: 'The Wood lies outside the walls of the Mansus. As any student of the Histories knows, the Mansus has no walls.'
readings.content: Illopoly describes how he came to make repeated visits to a dream-Wood via what he calls silver dreams. 'Trying to think your way to the Wood,' he explains, 'is like thinking your way to being in love. But I did find a Secret that helped.'

readings_cn.content: 伊利奥波里在书中描述了他如何通过他口中的银色梦境反复造访梦中的林地。“通过遐想到达林地，”他解释道，“如同遐想坠入爱河一般。不过我的确找到了有所裨助的秘密。”
readings_cn.intro: “林地生长于漫宿墙外。每一个研习诸史的人都知道，漫宿无墙。”

items.name: Travelling at Night, vol 2
items.description: The annotated dream-journals of Christopher Illopoly, sometimes called 'the only readable occultist': literate, entertaining, bewildering.
items.description_cn: 带注解的克里斯托弗·伊利奥波里的梦境手记，有时也被称为“唯一能读懂的密教典籍”：文笔精妙，富有趣味，扑朔迷离。

readings.intro: There is an extensive discussion of the comparisons between Illopoly's own dreams and those of the Emperor Elagabalus, who Illopoly regards as a dupe or avatar of the Sun-in-Rags. 'The White is west of the world,' Illopoly remarks, 'and Winter does not wait forever.'
readings.content: 'Elagabalus found his way to the White Door at last, thankfully. Speech can't pass the White Door, and honestly, Elagabalus never had anything very interesting to say. I tried to follow in his footsteps, but I never learnt enough of the White. I suppose I'm thankful for that, too. But here's what I do know...'

readings_cn.intro: 书中对伊利奥波里自身的梦境与皇帝埃拉伽巴路斯的梦境，两者间的相似处进行了大篇幅的讨论。伊利奥波里认为埃拉伽巴路斯是残阳的傀儡或化身。“纯白在世界以西，”伊利奥波里评论道，“且冬不永待。”
readings_cn.content: “谢天谢地，埃拉伽巴路斯最终寻见了纯白之门。言辞无法穿过纯白之门，而且说实话，埃拉伽巴路斯讲不出什么有趣的话。我曾经尝试追随他的脚步，但终究对纯白领会不足。大概我也幸而如此吧。但我确实知道……”

items.name: Travelling at Night, vol 3
items.description: The annotated dream-journals of Christopher Illopoly, sometimes called 'the only readable occultist': literate, entertaining, bewildering.
items.description_cn: 带注解的克里斯托弗·伊利奥波里的梦境手记，有时也被称为“唯一能读懂的密教典籍”：文笔精妙，富有趣味，扑朔迷离。

readings.intro: Illopoly's disquisitions on fire and the Unburnt God are interrupted by passages of distractingly erotic poetry addressed to 'Baldomera'.
readings.content: 'To reach the Stag Door, I believe that all you really need is to want something enough. But I've never wanted anything that much, except of course Baldomera, and I'm very much afraid that the knot in the story is this: what Baldomera wants is the Stag Door. But here's something I learnt in Persia. Perhaps it'll teach you what *you* want.'

readings_cn.content: “要去至牡鹿之门，我认为人需要的只是足够强烈想要某物的念头。可是我从来没有那样想要过什么，当然，除了对巴尔多梅姬，且这恐怕是此事的死结所在：巴尔多梅姬想要的是牡鹿之门。不过，下文是我在波斯学到的一些东西。或许能教会你想要何物。”
readings_cn.intro: 伊利奥波里在讨论火焰和不焚之神的论文中插入了数段致“巴尔多梅姬”的香艳诗文。

items.name: The Locksmith's Dream: a Light through the Keyhole
items.description: The first volume of Teresa Galmier's examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans.
items.description_cn: 特蕾莎·加尔米耶在书中考察了匠人们所经历的神秘梦境中的相似之处。丛书第一卷。

readings.intro: The parallels in mystic dreams experienced by carpenters, masons and other artisans, and what they purport to reveal about the architecture of the world. Surprisingly mordant and even funny. No-one has ever explained why Galmier devoted herself to this quixotic exploration of artisan's dreams.
readings.content: 'Time and again we hear of the Wood, which rises from the world's foundation. All trees reach for light. What does the Wood reach for? Is there a difference between light and Light? I think the key to dreams of the Wood might be one of these - the one that isn't exactly real.'

readings_cn.content: “我们一次次听说‘林地’，从世界的基盘升起的地方。一切树木都向光生长。而‘林地’之树向何生长？此光和彼‘光’有何区别？我认为通往林地梦境的钥匙或在答案当中——在不完全真实的那个答案中。”
readings_cn.intro: 木匠、泥瓦匠和其他工匠所经历的神秘梦境互有相似之处，他们自以为揭露出的世界之建构亦然。本书出人意料的辛辣，甚至有趣。没人解释得清加尔米耶为何热衷于对工匠的梦展开这种异想天开的探索。

items.name: The Locksmith's Dream: Portions and Proportions
items.description: The second volume of Teresa Galmier's examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans. The frontispiece has been slashed with a razor.
items.description_cn: 特蕾莎·加尔米耶在书中考察了匠人们所经历的神秘梦境中的相似之处。丛书第二卷。扉页已被人拿剃刀划烂。

readings.intro: In this volume, Galmier records fewer dreams, and explicates more of her own elaborate theories. 'We see this again and again: what is below can't escape what is above.'
readings.content: 'The finest artisans all dream of the White Door in the end. I'm no artisan, only a scholar. I think there's a Secret that all these artisans know, but I think that Secret is only half the story.'

readings_cn.intro: 加尔米耶在本卷中记录了数个梦境，进一步阐释了自己周详的理论。“我们反复看到这样一句话：下部无法脱离上部。”
readings_cn.content: “最杰出的工匠最后都梦到了纯白之门。我只是一名学者，而非工匠。我觉得一定存在一个所有这些工匠都知晓的秘密，不过我也觉得这个秘密只是其中的一半。”

items.name: The Locksmith's Dream: Trespasses
items.description: The third volume of Teresa Galmier's examination of parallels in the mystic dreams of artisans.
items.description_cn: 特蕾莎·加尔米耶在书中考察了匠人们所经历的神秘梦境中的相似之处。丛书第三卷。

readings.intro: In this volume, notoriously, Galmier's prose begins to disintegrate, and it is not clear which dreams are in fact her own.
readings.content: 'The woman in the sand-coloured robe has told me: the stairways of the Mansus go ever up. Death is down. The Mother of Ants guards both directions with each of her heads, and so the passage must always be through a wound. I think the White Door might be a wound. That's one reason the Dead sometimes pass it. I think I have the other half of the Secret now, and I hope my reader can put both halves together.'

readings_cn.content: “身着沙色长袍的女人告诉我：漫宿的阶梯一直朝上延伸。死亡则朝下。蚁母用她的两个头颅分别卫戍上下两方，若要通行，必须通过创口。我觉得纯白之门或许就是创口。这即是亡者有时从此门通过的一个原因。我觉得我找到另一半秘密了，我希望本书的读者能够将两半秘密拼合完整。”
readings_cn.intro: 众所周知，加尔米耶的文字从此卷开始语不成章，让人弄不清哪些梦境其实是她本人的。

items.name: The Six Letters on Necessity
items.description: Warnings and confessions about the cost of the secret arts, addressed to a student by the seventeenth-century magus (and reputed immortal) Julian Coseley
items.description_cn: 本书记载了对修习无形之术所付出代价的警告和忏悔，乃十七世纪的术士（据传亦是永生不死者）朱利安·科赛利馈赠学生之物。

readings.intro: Coseley's tone is urgent - as if he suspected he might have little time left.
readings.content: 'Even the Sunne can be divided, though it require the Forge of Dayes for its division.'

readings_cn.content: “即便是冭阳也能被分裂，尽管它要求㿟日铸炉动手。”
readings_cn.intro: 科赛利语气急迫——仿佛自疑时日无多。

items.name: The Victory of Crowns
items.description: Erratic accounts by 'Arun' of the hunting and consumption of supposed immortals by shadowy assassins. Published in the late nineteenth century.
items.description_cn: 一本怪书，作者署名“阿伦”。记载了某些不为人知的暗杀者们追猎和进食据称永生不死的人们的经过。出版于十九世纪后期。

readings.intro: The assassins are, according to 'Arun', the agents of a power called the Coronel, a 'soldier of the Secret Masters'. The accounts date back to Roman times.
readings.content: Arun's scholarship is dubious, but he (she?) writes pithily. Incidents of sudden and violent death are interspersed with aphorisms: 'Hours don't dream. Long try not to.'

readings_cn.intro: 据“阿伦”称，这些暗杀者是一位名为“尚校”的神灵的使者，是“隶属于诸位秘密大师的士兵”。此类说法一直可上溯至罗马时代。
readings_cn.content: 阿伦的学识令人存疑，但是他（或是她？）的文笔简洁有力，在记述突发且暴力的死亡事件时穿插着警句：“司辰无梦，长生者力图无梦。”

items.name: An Introduction to Histories
items.description: The seventeenth-century mystic and antiquarian Claude Hersault describes divergent incidents in five major Histories.
items.description_cn: 由十七世纪的神秘主义者兼古董商人克劳德·海索所著，描述了五大历史中的分歧事件。

readings.intro: The prologue warns at length of the iniquities of one Julian Coseley, a former colleague who Hersault now describes darkly as 'a Worm of Worms'. It seems Coseley advised Hersault early in the writing of the book, but Hersault later became suspicious.
readings.content: Hersault identifies Blood, Silver, Design and the Worms as the central axes of each of the Histories, and claims that the so-called Second History is the true one.

readings_cn.intro: 书的序言用长篇笔墨警告人们一个名为朱利安·科赛利的人的罪恶行径，海索将这位前同僚尖刻地描述成“蠕虫中的蠕虫”。海索貌似在本书创作的早期得到过科赛利的建议，后又对其起疑。
readings_cn.content: 海索认定各历史的中轴分别为血、银、设计和蠕虫，并称所谓的第二史才是真正的历史。

items.name: On the White
items.description: Solomon Husher writes, perhaps allegorically, of Winter, and its long slow doomed romance with the Sun. The epigraph is 'Sunset at Noon'.
items.description_cn: 所罗门·赫舍著，书的内容也许能解读为关于冬季的寓言，以及它与太阳漫长的，缓缓迎来毁灭的罗曼史。本书的引言是“午时日落”。

readings.intro: On closer investigation, the work seems to be a theory of aesthetics, or perhaps a set of warnings about the dangers of painting.
readings.content: Husher writes distractedly about his suspicion of colours and his yearning for death. He hints at a Great Work he has envisaged, or begun, where the 'palest of paintings' will enthral the world. He returns again and again to certain compelling phrases which he claims are the 'secret words of Winter'.

readings_cn.intro: 若仔细研究本书，可以发现其内容似乎是一种美学理论，又或者是对绘画之危险的一系列警告。
readings_cn.content: 赫舍在书中心烦意乱地写下了他对颜色的疑问和对死亡的渴求。他还略微提及他正在构思，或已开始实践的那件大作——“淡白至极的绘画”将令世界为之着迷。他一遍遍重复着某几句引人注目的话，他称之为“冬之密文”。

items.name: The Humours of a Gentleman
items.description: Samuel Savage's satirical comedy, on the intrigues of the ailing, but cunning John Sonne, his mistress Maevelin, her lover Leo, and the upstart Corvino.
items.description_cn: 萨缪尔·萨维奇所著的讽刺喜剧，主要角色包括身体抱恙然却狡诈多端的约翰·泰扬，他的情妇琅优，琅优的情人施梓，还有暴发户乌亚。

readings.intro: By the end of the first act, Maevelin has revealed a secret door in the walls of the House to Leo, and Corvino has taken to consuming Worms.
readings.content: The play is scabrous and occasionally hilarious. The characters are contrary and capricious. Many of the more resonant lines might well be formulae of power, disguised in plain sight.

readings_cn.intro: 在第一幕结尾，琅优向施梓透露居屋的墙上有秘门，而乌亚则开始惯于进食蠕虫。
readings_cn.content: 这部戏剧于粗俗间或又令人捧腹。戏中角色相互对立而又反复无常。其中多句更加意有所指的台词或可用于施展强力的法术，尽管它们藏于平平无奇的场景之中。

items.name: The Queens of the Rivers
items.description: A surreal contemporary play by the enigmatic Monica Medina, in which the Queens of the Rivers are murdered, one by one.
items.description_cn: 一部超现实风格的当代戏剧，作者是名为莫妮卡·麦地那的神秘人物。剧中的诸位河川女王一一为人所杀。

readings.intro: The Queen of the Vistula is poisoned. The Queen of the Dnieper chokes on a fish-hook. The Queen of the Tagus is burnt alive...
readings.content: The culprit, it transpires, is the audience. The surviving Queens are directed to execute whatever audience members do not escape. A surprisingly lucid epilogue suggests that the correspondence of river-names with historical events does provide clues to secret histories behind our own.

readings_cn.intro: 维斯瓦河女王被毒死。第聂伯河女王被鱼钩呛死。塔霍河女王被活活烧死……
readings_cn.content: 真相大白，杀人真凶正是台下的观众。剧本要求存活的女王处死所有未逃走的观众。一段清醒到令人意外的收场白提示说，河川之名与历史事件间的对应关系实为一种线索，可供探究我们所在的历史背后的隐秘历史。

items.name: Apollo and Marsyas
items.description: The libretto of a lost opera concerning the contest between Apollo and Marsyas, and its tragic outcome. The librettist is identified only by their initials.
items.description_cn: 某部失传歌剧的唱本，题材为阿波罗和马西亚斯之间的比试及此事的悲剧结局。唱词作者只留下了名字的首字母缩写。

readings.intro: In the original myth, Marsyas lost the musical contest and was flayed by Apollo, who later regretted it. In this version, Marsyas' skin has a further history...
readings.content: The Skin of Marsyas gives oracles, and is later smuggled to Phrygia, where the priestesses of Cybele use it for a drum. At the climax, the striking of the drum drives would-be violators of the priestess to suicidal madness. The opera ends with a wistful hymn from the youngest priestess on the beauty of mountain pines.

readings_cn.intro: 在原本的神话中，马西亚斯因在音乐比试中败给了阿波罗而被剥皮，阿波罗事后亦为此后悔。在这个版本中，马西亚斯的皮有着更深层的历史……
readings_cn.content: 马西亚斯的皮拥有给予神谕之力，后被偷运至弗里吉亚，让库柏勒的女祭司作成了鼓面。在歌剧的高潮，这面鼓的震响将想要侵犯女祭司之人逼疯至自杀。最后，歌剧在最年幼的女祭司赞颂山松之美的忧愁歌声中收尾。

items.name: The Skeleton Songs
items.description: Poems of greedy delight composed by the possibly pseudonymous Arabella Dusk, the rumoured heiress-turned-madam-turned-poetess.
items.description_cn: 一部咏颂贪婪享乐的诗集，作者是传闻中从女继承人成为贵妇又成为诗人的阿拉贝拉·达斯克，该名很可能是伪名。

readings.intro: In Arabella's introduction, she explains that the book was to be illustrated, but that the Suppression Bureau would not permit it. She hints that the illustrations still exist somewhere. The book is dedicated to 'Sir Parsival of the Red Cup'.
readings.content: The Twenty-Six Delightful Fruits; the Seven Chastisements; the Nine Gardens; the Four Regrets.

readings_cn.intro: 阿拉贝拉在引言中解释说，她这本书本应有插图，但防剿局不会允许。她暗示插图仍存于某处。本书是致“寻找赤杯的帕西瓦尔爵士”的献礼。
readings_cn.content: 二十六颗悦人的果实，七种责罚，九座花园，四桩悔事。

items.name: The Orchid Transfigurations: a Feast
items.description: A compilation of quasi-Rosicrucian allegories, supposedly by Robert Fludd. This is in the original Latin.
items.description_cn: 一部玫瑰十字会式寓言的合集，据称为罗伯特·福路德著。此为其拉丁语原著。

readings.intro: The illustrations are certainly striking. They flush the skin and glow beneath the eyelids after the book is closed.
readings.content: 'We must devour to be devoured. We cannot be undevoured, as we cannot be unborn.'

readings_cn.intro: 本书的插图确实夺人眼球；使人面色潮红，即使合上书页仍在眼底印照不去。
readings_cn.content: “人必先噬人，而后人噬之。为人噬者不可逆，如人之诞世不可逆。”

items.name: The Orchid Transfigurations: Noon
items.description: The third volume of a compilation of quasi-Rosicrucian allegories, supposedly by Robert Fludd. This is in the original Latin.
items.description_cn: 一部玫瑰十字会式寓言的合集，推测为罗伯特·福路德所著，丛书第三卷。此为其拉丁语原著。

readings.intro: A long dialogue between the Mountain-Mother and the Vigilant Storm describes the ways in which both mountains and storms end, and the protections they use against those ends.
readings.content: 'But we must use the knife,' said the Lion-Throned One, 'the noose, the flame, the Waking Word, against those who have passed the Three-Valved Door. And so none may pass: that is our Law, and the Law of the Sun.'

readings_cn.intro: 一段“山峦之母”与“警醒风暴”间的长对话，描述了山峦与风暴的下场，也描述了他们如何规避此类下场。
readings_cn.content: “然我们须用刀、”以狮背为王座者说，“绞索、火焰、唤醒之语对抗穿过三膜之门者。令无人可从此处通过：这是我们的法则，也是太阳的法则。”

items.name: The Orchid Transfigurations: a Birth
items.description: The second volume of a compilation of quasi-Rosicrucian allegories, supposedly by Robert Fludd. This is in the original Latin.
items.description_cn: 一部玫瑰十字会式寓言的合集，推测为罗伯特·福路德所著，丛书第二卷。此为其拉丁语原著。

readings.intro: Fludd, or pseudo-Fludd, suggests alignments between the alchemical tradition of rubedo and the older Grail traditions, through the Pine-Knight's quest for the Cinnabar Cup.
readings.content: Seek the Cup in the birthing-bed,' the Pine-Knight is told. The Midwife at the birthing-bed, to his amazement, is the Mountain-Mother. In a fit of awe, he both gelds and flays himself. The Vigilant Storm bursts joyfully from the remains.

readings_cn.intro: 福路德，或自称福路德者，以松树骑士寻找朱砂杯的故事暗示了炼金术传统的“红化”之法与更古老的圣杯传承间的对应关系。
readings_cn.content: “‘于产床中寻觅朱砂杯’，这是交给松树骑士的任务。令他惊奇的是，产床旁的助产士竟是山峦之母。带着敬畏之情，他阉割了自己，并将自己的皮剥下。警醒风暴欢乐地从他的残躯中冲出。”

items.name: De Bellis Murorum
items.description: An eighteenth-century epic poem by the pseudonymous 'Solipsistos'.
items.description_cn: 十八世纪的史诗，作者托名为“索利浦西斯托斯”。

readings.intro: The poem elliptically describes a war between beasts, weather phenomena, and arcane concepts. It's quite specific about their tactics.
readings.content: 'The Two-One joined, and the Horned distinguished. Consequently, blood.'

readings_cn.intro: 这首诗概括性地描写了野兽、天气现象、神秘概念三者间的战争。战术部分写得相当具体。
readings_cn.content: “二一相合，角者得彰。于是得血。”

items.name: On What is Contained By Silver
items.description: A dire bestiary of the horrors to be found in mirrors. This is a recent edition of a third century text by 'Poemander'.
items.description_cn: 一部可怕的动物寓言集，讲述了现于镜面的恐怖。由“牧人者”著于三世纪，这个版本是近年新出的。

readings.intro: Poemander engages in a considerable and pedantic discussion about the particular mirror-alloys that attract particular danger from particular entities. This is less useful, of course, in an era where most mirrors are silvered glass.
readings.content: 'The virgins/maidens of the mirror favour orchids. The [behindlings?] favour the rhododendron. Cut flowers of either nature should not be placed before polished bronze.'

readings_cn.intro: “牧人者”就“用特定合金制成的镜面会有吸引特定的危险实体的风险”这一主题进行了长篇累牍的、学究式的讨论。当然，在一个绝大多数镜子都用上了镀银层的时代，这些探讨就显得不那么有用了。
readings_cn.content: “镜中的处女/少女偏好兰花，而[镜后之灵？]则偏爱杜鹃花。两种花在剪下后都不该放在抛亮的青铜器前。”

items.name: A True and Complete Accounting of the Asclepian Mysteries of the Roots of the House
items.name_cn: 《对居屋根基的阿斯克利庇之谜真实而完整的记述》
items.description: Descriptions of the 'Asclepian Mysteries', reproduced by one 'Rylee Grese' from - supposedly - a much older text. It's unlikely to be genuine, but it makes a reference to 'The House without Walls and its Wood' right there in the prologue.
items.description_cn: 本书记述了“阿斯克利庇之谜”，是一部——据推测——更古老的文献的复制本，制作者署名“李利·格里斯”。书的内容不太可信，然而其在序言即明确提及了“无墙的居屋及其所伴的林地”。

readings.intro: This is very obviously not an antique text. At the very least, it has been badly mutilated. But it contains substantial intriguing material: especially, a persuasive comparison of the House without Walls, without doors to the human body, with its many portals.
readings.content: 'The direction of Death is down,' the book explains. 'The Peacock Door has been considered a rent, or an abrasion, but in some respects is more like a mouth - if not a more treasured point of entry.' Discussions of the Doors include a rite which may conjure creatures through those doors, although key incantations are missing.

readings_cn.intro: 本书很显然并非古卷，顶多称得上十分破旧。但书中记录了大量有意思的素材，特别是这样一个很有说服力的对比：将无墙无门的居屋在“有诸多入口”这一点上与拥有七窍的人体相比较。
readings_cn.content: “死亡的方向朝下，”书中这样解释，“孔雀之门被认为是一种裂缝，或是一处磨损。但从其他角度看，它更像是一张嘴——或者说是一种更珍贵的入口。”对门扉的讨论中包括了一种通过这些门召唤生物的仪式，虽然缺失了关键祷词。

items.name: Wainscot Histories
items.description: Subtitled 'Stories from Behind the Walls': a miscellany of non-traditional histories, including battles not generally acknowledged and countries which appear on no map, told in a playful, apparently fictional manner.
items.description_cn: 一本关于非常规历史的杂录，副标题为“发生在墙壁背后的故事”。书中记有数个不广为人知的战役和从未载于地图的国家，文风戏谑，明显带有虚构成分。
