readings.content: 'It is essential that these Protections be completed every fourth year, to defend against the entry of the Worms and against the avidity of the Wave and the Wound.' In the current History at least, there is no indication that these Protections have been performed regularly for at least the last thousand years.

readings_cn.intro: 艾丽在本书中描述了能用于各种情况的强大保护咒。
readings_cn.content: “重要的是，这些保护咒需每四年补修一次，以抵御蠕虫进入以及‘水波’和‘创口’的热盼。”至少在现今这重历史中，过去至少一千年内没有迹象表明有人定期施放过这些保护咒。

items.name: The Time of Division
items.description: In which Amira Zahra prophesies the events later known as the Intercalate, when the Hour called Sun-in-Splendour will be divided.
items.description_cn: 阿米拉·扎拉在本书中预言了后人称为“置闰”的事件：名为骄阳的司辰被分裂。

readings.intro: The Sun will be divided that it might not sire children. Still its children shall be Four in number and its children shall be Seven in number and its children shall also be Numberless. The Numberless shall open the way for the Seven, and the Seven shall consume the Four...'
readings.content: Amira prophesies four great wars before the Second Dawn, when the Sun-in-Splendour shall rise again. She cautions: 'Sunrise is blood, and I foretell now that the Sun shall rise from blood, yet not the colour of the blood, nor the hour of Night.' She includes a rite that she speculates will be necessary for the Second Dawn.

readings_cn.intro: “太阳将遭分裂，故它许不能再生产子嗣。即便如此，其子嗣之数应为四再其子嗣之数应为七再其子嗣之数更应不可计数。不可计数者将为七者打开道路，七者将摄食四者……”
readings_cn.content: 阿米拉预卜了“第二拂晓”，即骄阳再度升起前的四场大战。她提醒道：“日出为血，我于此预言骄阳将从血中升起，却既无鲜血的颜色，亦非夜晚的时辰。”她给出了她推测第二拂晓所需的一个仪式。

items.name: A Manual for Departure
items.description: The author, who identifies itself as the Jekadu, claims to be one of the Great Hooded Princes of the Land of the River. The style is informal, even chatty.
items.description_cn: 作者自称杰卡杜，为圣河流域的兜颈贵胄之一。文风并不正式，甚至可说像闲聊。

readings.intro: 'No, these doors shouldn't be recorded, but if we had only recorded things before we'd had to leave the Fifth History, we would be in a much better state. So here I am writing it down, and if you don't like it you can sanction me.'
readings.content: The 'Manual for Departure' lists a number of strategies - occult, martial and political - for quick escapes. Many are irrelevant, obsolete or enigmatic, but the Manual does include a number of powerful techniques for opening portals.

readings_cn.content: 《脱身手册》列举了若干——密教上，军事上和政治上的——快速脱逃策略。其中许多是可有可无，过时落后或高深难懂的，但这本手册的确给出了若干强力的开启门洞的技术。
readings_cn.intro: “不，不应该记录这些门，但如果那时，我们在被迫离开第五史前做了记录，我们现在的景况会好得多。所以我现在将其付诸笔端，如果你不喜欢，你可以制裁我。”

items.name: Inaam, Kapigiginlupir, Garkie, Cryppys
items.name_cn: 《伊纳姆、卡皮吉吉努皮尔、加尔基、克雷皮斯》
items.description: In which four enigmatic figures tell the stories they've heard over the years at the Roost, the secret location where the aviform Hours congregate.
items.description_cn: 书中的四个神秘人物讲述了他们多年来在“栖木”——鸟形司辰的集会地——听到的故事。

readings.intro: INAAM: Has not the Beach-Crow shared his treasures? GARKIE: Not the rarest. He takes those things most precious, which he claims found, not stolen.
readings.content: The Beach-Crow, Kapigiginlupir suggests, is not only a thief, but also a spy and even a voyeur. He has hidden the memory of secret couplings among the Hours and their Names in the corners of the House, as treasures to gloat over. There is particularly fevered speculation on a liaison between the Ring-Yew, that fervent hour of the Wood, and the Mare-in-the-Tree, who sometimes has been the Witch's Sister.

readings_cn.content: 卡皮吉吉努皮尔认为拾滩鸦不仅是盗贼，同时也是探子，甚至喜欢窥淫。他把司辰和祂们的具名者间秘密交合的记忆藏在居屋的角落，作为暗中夸耀的宝藏。还有一个很狂热的猜测：热情如火的林地司辰环杉，和有时与女巫做姐妹的树中牝马，这两者间有私情。
readings_cn.intro: 伊纳姆：拾滩鸦没有分享他的宝藏吗？加尔基：没有分享最稀有的。他把最珍贵的留给自己了，号称那些是他找到的，不是偷来的。

items.name: The Voyages of Ferninshun of Oreol
items.description: The impossible travels of a sea-captain of the late Phoenician era. Suppressed throughout recorded history: those who read it were said to disappear.
items.description_cn: 记载了一位船长在晚期腓尼基时代的不可能之旅。本书在有记载的历史中一直被封锁：读过这本书的人都消失了。

readings.intro: Ferninshun clearly visited the Mansus, sailing the length of the Painted River. He also claims to have traversed a sea of finest sand, to have dared the blazing waves of the Sun's surface, and to have descended to an underworld ocean lit by lamps of black nephrite...
readings.content: Ferninshun's final voyage is to retirement on a peaceful island across an evening sea, where he identifies a spring whose waters will keep him safe. 'I will be forgotten,' he declares, 'and this work my only trace.'

readings_cn.intro: 斐宁舜显然在沿画中之河航行时拜访过漫宿。他还称他横渡过沙滩最细腻的海域，挑战过太阳表面的热浪，也曾下潜到由墨玉照亮的地底之海……
readings_cn.content: 在最后一次远航中，斐宁舜跨越了薄暮之海，到一座平静的岛屿上安度余生。他认为那里有一眼能保证他的安全的泉水。“人们会忘记我，”他宣称，“而这本书将是我留下的唯一痕迹。”

items.name: The Scar in the Sky
items.description: Nyn wrote this, and came to regret it.
items.description_cn: 作者宁在写下本书后追悔不迭。

readings.intro: Each page of this book contains one word only, but as each page is turned, a knowledge creeps in.
readings.content: The final page is crowded. Each reader of the book records the same word. Now it is my turn.

readings_cn.intro: 这本书每一页只写有一个词，但每翻过一页，便有一个知识潜入脑中。
readings_cn.content: 最后一页写得满满当当。书的每个读者都会在此处记下同一个词。现在轮到我了。

items.name: A Seventh Voice
items.description: Samuel Savage's cycle of comic poems about a band of players who double as footpads seeking a seventh member.
items.description_cn: 萨缪尔·萨维奇创作的喜剧组诗，讲述了一支兼为路匪的乐队物色第七名成员的故事。

readings.intro: Sir Snatch-Sea is distracted by Mistress Twitch-Shell kissing Mistress Nether-Pearls, and fails to see Master Magglepie making off with the players' funds…
readings.content: The whole enterprise almost ends in disaster when Mistress Wander-Eye's family insults her costume, and she burns down their house in a fit of pique, but the day is finally saved by the Seventh Voice, a wandering book-monger who returns the band's lost music.

readings_cn.intro: 挛贝小姐狂热地吻着阴珠小姐，弄得窥海爵士分了心，完全没注意到希阙大师带着整支乐队的积蓄逃之夭夭……
readings_cn.content: 当游眸小姐的家人侮辱她的打扮时，乐队的事业几乎以灾难性的结果告终——她一怒之下将他们的房子付之一炬。但最后，这天被第七音拯救了，一位恰巧路过此处的图书商人归还了乐队丢失的音乐。

items.name: The Other Line
items.description: One of Samuel Savage's more thoughtful works: an allegorical play about the City Clarity, a city that is also a book, and the sentences which inhabit it.
items.description_cn: 萨缪尔·萨维奇最具思想性的作品之一：一部关于“明晰”城里的讽喻剧，这座城市本身也是一本书，同时又是书里的句子。

readings.intro: The Lords Proverbial and Lords Disquisitional war in the streets of Clarity, while the Punctuants get drunk on ink and supply the jokes (though, by Savage's usual standards, there aren't very many jokes.)
readings.content: The final act sees the Lords Proverbial unsealing the City Clarity's gate to expel the population into the unknown. (The formula that they use for the unsealing is a real one - it can be used with Knock and Preliminal Meter to create a gate-sign of power.)

readings_cn.intro: “谚语”勋爵与“学术”勋爵在“明晰”的街头爆发了战争，与此同时，其他“标点”们则醉饮墨水，讲着各种笑话（虽然就萨维奇一贯的标准来说，这些笑话并不算多）。
readings_cn.content: 剧本的最后一幕是“谚语”勋爵打开“明晰”的城门，把所有人驱逐到了未知之处。（剧中角色用于开门时的法术是真实存在的——将“阈前格律”与启一起使用，可创造出具有力量的门关符印。）

items.name: A Novel Method for Invocation & Contrition
items.description: Ingenious and rather beautiful techniques for entreating the Names of the Hours, developed by Rory Morrow, who styled himself 'the Sage-Knight'.
items.description_cn: 一系列巧妙且颇为优美的技术，用于向诸司辰的具名者请愿，由自称“睿智骑士”的罗里·莫罗发明。

readings.intro: The techniques rely on the unique qualities of the Ericapaean tongue. Morrow professes himself surprised that they serve better to entreat the Names of the Vagabond than the Names of Lantern or Winter Hours…
readings.content: Morrow demonstrates that Preliminal Meter techniques can be used with sufficient Rose to invoke the Vagabond's Names, transforming an Enduring Reflection into 'something wider of sky.'

readings_cn.intro: 这种技术高度依赖于厄里卡帕奥语的独特语调。莫罗自己也诧异它们为何更适合拜请浪游旅人的具名者，而不是灯或冬之司辰的具名者……
readings_cn.content: 莫罗论述道，“阙前格律”之技术可以与足够的引一起使用，来向浪游旅人的具名者请愿，将弥久映像转变为某种“来自天空的更广阔之物”。

items.name: Calicite Supplications
items.description: Prayers addressed to the Red Grail by the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot.
items.description_cn: 三重绳结姐妹会献给赤杯的祷文。

readings.intro: 'If we should remember not, let our children remember, in their redmost dreams…'
readings.content: One prayer describes how sufficient Grail-aspect can be used with Tridesma Hiera rites to give 'a life, a little life, a little little life' to a doll twisted from fabric…

readings_cn.intro: “假若我们未能记起，那就让我们的孩子记起，在他们最猩红的梦里……”
readings_cn.content: 其中一篇祷文描述了如何在足够的杯相下，用“三重誓之仪”来赋予一个用布料捻成的娃娃“生命，些许生命，些许渺小的生命”……

items.name: Ascite Supplications
items.description: Prayers addressed to the Horned-Axe by the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot.
items.description_cn: 三重绳结姐妹会献给双角斧的祷文。

readings.intro: 'If we should pass not, let our enemies pass, unto their deserved end…'
readings.content: One prayer describes how sufficient Moon-aspect can be used with Tridesma Hiera with almost any egg to hatch 'the Stone's children, the Sky's daughters, the Sea's sons.'

readings_cn.intro: “假若我们未能通过，那就让我们的敌人通过，落得他们应有的下场……”
readings_cn.content: 其中一篇祷文描述了如何在足够的月相下，用“三重誓之仪”从几乎任何卵中孵化出“岩石的子嗣、天空的女儿，大海的儿子”。

items.name: Malachite Supplications
items.description: Prayers addressed to the Malachite by the Sisterhood of the Triple Knot.
items.description_cn: 三重绳结姐妹会献给石绿的祷文。

readings.intro: 'If we should flourish not, let our enemies flourish, in that time when we are no more…'
readings.content: One prayer describes how a strong degree of Nectar-aspect can be used with Leathy and Tridesma Hiera rites to bring forth 'the Last Nectar of the Last History, the Living Ink, the Ink-in-Secret…'

readings_cn.intro: “假若我们未能繁盛，那就让我们的敌人繁盛，在我们不复存在之后……”
readings_cn.content: 其中一篇祷文描述了如何在足够的蜜相下，用“三重誓之仪”从遗忘之水中提取出“最后历史的最后之蜜，焕发生机之墨，隐秘之墨……”

items.name: The Sun's Lament
items.description: The first volume of the meditations of Abbot Thomas of the Abbey of the Black Dove.
items.description_cn: 黑鸽修道院院长托马斯的沉思录，第一卷。

readings.intro: 'The thorn-beaked crows took my eyes from me in justice for my crimes, but though I lost my Sight, I found my Light.'
readings.content: Abbot Thomas speaks of the breaking of his oaths to his sword-brother Trygve, and to the 'Lord of Scars' that he served before he came to the Abbey. He writes of the power of oath-bonds, and considers the means and morality of their sundering.

readings_cn.intro: “尖嘴群鸦为了惩罚我的罪行，啄掉了我的双眼。虽然我失去了视力，却因此找到自己的光明。”
readings_cn.content: 托马斯院长谈到在来到修道院之前，他如何背弃了与自己的剑兄特里格夫，以及他曾经侍奉过的“伤疤之主”的誓言。他也提到了誓言的约束力，探讨了解除这种关系的方法和道德问题。

items.name: The Wind's Ruin
items.description: The second volume of the meditations of Abbot Thomas of the Abbey of the Black Dove.
items.description_cn: 黑鸽修道院院长托马斯的沉思录，第二卷。

readings.intro: Abbot Thomas speaks of his time as a raider, when his name was not Thomas but Toke, 'scything the sea, striving for plunder'…
readings.content: Abbot Thomas clearly regrets his 'storm-years', and much of the book is taken up with his thoughts on penitence; but there are hints also that he misses those years, and the companionship of his 'sword-brother, ship-brother' Trygve.

readings_cn.intro: 托马斯院长回忆了他曾为海盗的那段时光，那时他的名字还是托克，而不是托马斯，“叱咤海上，醉心掠夺”……
readings_cn.content: 托马斯院长确实为自己的“风暴岁月”忏悔，书中的大部分篇幅也饱含他的忏悔之意；但也有迹象表明，他依然怀念那段时光，怀念他的“剑兄与船弟”特里格夫的陪伴。

items.name: The Moon's Egg
items.description: The third and last volume of the meditations of Abbot Thomas of the Abbey of the Black Dove.
items.description_cn: 黑鸽修道院院长托马斯的沉思录，第三卷。

readings.intro: Abbot Thomas speaks of the coming death he hears in the sound of the waves, but rejoices that his blood will water the 'Egg of the Moon' - by which he seems to mean the future.
readings.content: The last chapter was dictated, not written, by Abbot Thomas. When Thomas' old sword-brother Trygve returned to raid the Abbey, Thomas had broken his monastic oaths and taken up arms to defend the abbey. The two had both been mortally wounded. Thomas' last words are 'The Wheel turns; the Moon sleeps.'

readings_cn.intro: 托马斯院长说起他在涛声中听见了自己迫近的死亡，但又为自己的鲜血即将浇灌“月亮之卵”而感到欣喜——他指的似乎是未来之事。
readings_cn.content: 最后一章由托马斯院长口述，而非他亲笔写就。当他昔日的剑兄特里格夫袭击修道院时，托马斯打破了身为修士的誓言，为了保卫修道院再次拿起武器。两人都在战斗中身负重伤。托马斯的遗言是：“转轮转动；月亮沉眠”。

items.name: The Black Book of Brittany
items.description: A volume of ink-lore gifted to St Brandan's by Brian of Brittany, who was made Earl of Cornwall after the Norman Conquest.
items.description_cn: 布列塔尼的布莱恩在诺曼征服后被封为康沃尔伯爵，这是他赠予圣布伦丹修道院的关于墨水秘传的卷册。

readings.intro: ''The Black Flower lies heavy, but the roots of the Watchman's Tree run deep, and they may not be hidden forever…'
readings.content: The Black Flower, spoken of as a doom or geas, can be held at bay with the Last Ink of Power - brewed from 'the Pale Mixture' in the presence of sufficient Winter with the arts of Containment.

readings_cn.intro: “黑花压覆，但守夜人之树的根须向下深扎，它们也许无法永远被掩藏……”
readings_cn.content: 本书似乎把黑花描述为某种厄运或灾难，并声称它可以用最后的力量之墨控制。这种墨水可以在足够的冬下，用收容之技艺从“苍白的混合物”中提取。

items.name: The White Book of Brittany
items.description: A volume of death-lore gifted to St Brandan's by Brian of Brittany, who was made Earl of Cornwall after the Norman Conquest.
items.description_cn: 布列塔尼的布莱恩在诺曼征服后被封为康沃尔伯爵，这是他赠予圣布伦丹修道院的关于死亡密传的卷册。

readings.intro: 'The White Flower lies heavy, but the roots of the Watchman's Tree run deeper than snow...'
readings.content: The White Flower is described as the 'death of wisdom' - but wisdom can pass into sleep, not death, when 'the Rage of Glass' is subjected to sufficiently powerful Winter-aspect while the Ragged Crossroads arts are invoked.

readings_cn.intro: “白花压覆，但守夜人之树的根须深过积雪……”
readings_cn.content: 白花在文中被描述为“智慧的死亡”——但智慧可以进入沉睡（而不是死亡），只要在足够的冬相下，用“残破十字路”处理“玻璃的盛怒”……

items.name: The Red Book of Brittany
items.description: A volume of ink-lore gifted to St Brandan's by Brian of Brittany, who was made Earl of Cornwall after the Norman Conquest.
items.description_cn: 布列塔尼的布莱恩在诺曼征服后被封为康沃尔伯爵，这是他赠予圣布伦丹修道院的关于墨水秘传的卷册。

readings.intro: 'The Red Flower lies heavy, but the roots of the Watchman's Tree are constant…''
readings.content: The Red Flower is described as 'the temptation of suffering'; but its suffering can apparently be allayed when 'the Copper Fruit' is enspelled with Nectar-aspect alongside Herbs and Infusions techniques. A variant of the same approach, with the Inks of Power techniques outlined here, can 'gentle Leathy into a Great Ink...'

readings_cn.intro: “红花压覆，但守夜人之树的根须亘古不变……”
readings_cn.content: 红花在文中被描述为“苦痛的诱惑”；但这种苦痛可以被抑制，只需将“铜色果实”佐以足够的蜜相，用“草药与药汤”技术进行处理。而如果使用本书中列明的“力量之墨”技术，则会将“遗忘之水柔化成一种伟大的墨水……”

items.name: The Mirror of Melancthe
items.description: The day-book and dream-journal of Abbess Melancthe, venerated as a saint and respected as an alchemist.
items.description_cn: 梅兰瑟院长的日记簿和梦境记录。她既作为圣人受人崇拜，也作为炼金术士受人尊敬。

readings.intro: Melancthe speaks longingly of 'those we would call from behind the sky…'
readings.content: Melancthe claims that the Sights and Sensations arts that she describes can be used to invoke 'the Dream of a Star', when sufficient Sky-aspect is invoked to uplift an Ascendant Harmony.

readings_cn.intro: 梅兰瑟满怀渴望地叙述“那些我们会从天空之后唤来的存在……”
readings_cn.content: 梅兰瑟声称，她在本书中描述的“景象与感知”之技艺，辅以足够的穹相，可以把一段方兴和声扬升为“星辰的梦”。

items.name: A Descent of the Shell
items.description: A treatise on eggs, light, and optics by Abbess Melancthe, dazzlingly illuminated with renderings of the Abbess' visions.
items.description_cn: 梅兰瑟院长关于卵、光源与光学的专著。院长对自身幻象的描写将本书渲染得令人眼花缭乱。

readings.intro: The book is unexpectedly challenging to read. The bright glitter of the gold-leaf illuminations acquires a migrainous quality; the eye aches and tires…
readings.content: This is, most likely, the 'certain vivid book' that Melancthe once sent to Gunnhild, daughter of King Harold, which provoked in her 'a dream of eyes' but also caused her to begin to lose her sight (until she was healed by the saint-bishop Wulfstan). To complete it is a kind of test. Its double thesis, at last, seems to be that the Sun is either an eye or an egg; and so the Second Dawn will be either its opening, or its hatching.

readings_cn.content: 本书极可能就是梅兰瑟曾赠与哈罗德国王的女儿——冈希尔德的“那本亮丽的书”，不仅唤起了她的“眼之梦”，也导致了她日后的失明（直到她被圣伍尔夫斯坦主教治愈）。阅读此书本身就是一种挑战。本书最后得出的双重论点似乎是：太阳要么是眼瞳，要么是卵；故而第二拂晓将是它的睁开或者孵化。
readings_cn.intro: 本书意外地难以阅读。饰有金箔的耀眼内页使本书带上了某种易使人偏头痛的性质；眼睛很快便会又涩又干……

items.name: Against Vitruvius
items.description: A fourteenth-century treatise on esoteric mechanics and parahydraulics by Abbot Ranulph, best known now as a mason-architect.
items.description_cn: 成书于十四世纪的一本关于深奥的力学与泛水力学的专著，作者拉努尔夫院长以石匠兼建筑师的身份广为人知。

readings.intro: Ranulph describes how he tested some of these techniques in the construction of the Winter Tower (now called the Long Tower). He admits to unexpected consequences…
readings.content: Ranulph mentions that the tower of Ely Cathedral collapsed around the time the Winter Tower was completed… although he stops short of suggesting that one was the cause of another. 'A tower falls, a tower rises,' is all he'll commit to.

readings_cn.intro: 拉努尔夫在书中谈及他是如何在建造冬塔（现在被称为长生者塔）的时候实践了这些技术的某些内容的。他承认，这产生了些意想不到的后果……
readings_cn.content: 拉努尔夫提到，伊利大教堂的塔楼在冬塔竣工的那段时期倒塌了……尽管他在点明两者之间的因果关系前停下了笔。“一塔倒坍，一塔攀升”，这就是他所承诺的全部。

items.name: De motu corporum vetitorum
items.description: The author rejoices in the name of 'Abelard Hubris', and the title might be translated as 'On the Forbidden Motions of Bodies' - evidently a reference to Newton's 'De Motu Corporem', published some twenty years previously.
items.description_cn: 作者似乎十分中意于“亚伯拉德·修伯里斯”这个笔名，而本书的标题可大致译为“论物体被禁止之运动”——很明显意指牛顿于约二十年前发表的论文《De Motu Corporem》（《论物体之运动》）。

readings.intro: Hubris's thesis: that stars, planets and other bodies are the proxies or even essences of the Hours, and that conjunctions and occlusions reveal the outcome of Hour-intrigues in the Mansus.
readings.content: Hubris declares that the Great Comet of 1577 was the physical embodiment of the Hour named Madrugad; that It disintegrated but its fragments gravitate to bone-marrow, where they can be located even now. He insists that Ouranoscopic techniques can be used with Essential Periost and sufficient Sky to create a 'talisman gerifugic'.

readings_cn.intro: 修伯里斯的论点是：恒星、行星及其他天体是司辰的代理，或者甚至是司辰的本质，而它们的合相与掩星则能够反映出漫宿司辰间的私通与阴谋。
readings_cn.content: 修伯里斯宣称1577年的大彗星是名为昕旦的司辰在物质世界的化身；它已分解，但它的碎片会被骨髓吸引，时至今日，骨髓里也依旧有它们的残留。他坚称“窥天术”之技术可以与骨本精华及足够的穹一同使用，来制造出一种“延命护身符”。

items.name: The Instruments of the Heart
items.description: Sister Isabel, then Precentress of the Abbey-Church of St Brandan's, engages in dialogues with a Heart-long of a kind called 'duendrazon' that has taken partial possession of her body.
items.description_cn: 时任圣布伦丹修道院女领唱一职的伊莎贝尔修女，与一名位列“叩心魅”的心之长生者间进行的对谈。后者当时已部分占据了她的身体。

readings.intro: The duendrazon, like all its kind, usually dwells in the Mansus but can enter the physical world by manifesting as music, and take possession of a willing - or semi-willing - mortal who hears and loves that music… like Isabella.
readings.content: Isabella records her dreams of the high Mansus, where she is accorded the duendrazon's status and titles. In return, the duendrazon enjoys what it calls 'caesura' - a welcome oblivion. 'Our mostly-blessing is that we may never cease - except in caesurae'. There is something more that Isabella refers to as the 'caesura magna', but she laments that her duendrazon will not tell her exactly what that might be.

readings_cn.intro: 就像它的所有同类那样，叩心魅通常居住在漫宿中，但也能够以音乐的形式进入物质世界，并占据一个自愿（或是半自愿）的听到并喜爱那种音乐的凡人的身体……比如伊莎贝尔。
readings_cn.content: 伊莎贝尔记录了她在漫宿的高处所见的梦境——在那里她被暂时赋予了叩心魅的头衔与地位。作为回报，叩心魅在物质世界享受着它所谓的“音顿”——一种无拘无束的混沌状态。“我们最大的幸事便是我们永不休止——除了在音顿之中。”伊莎贝尔还提到了一种她称之为“强音顿”的概念，但她也哀叹，她的叩心魅不会告诉她那具体是什么。

items.name: Journal of Thomas Dewulf
items.description: Thomas Dewulf, 2nd Baron Brancrug, was nicknamed 'Baron Silence of Castle Silence' for his taciturn severity - most likely the origin, eventually, of the name 'Hush House'.
items.description_cn: 托马斯·德沃尔夫，第二代布兰库格男爵，因其严厉且寡言而得到了“沉默城堡的沉默男爵”的称号——“噤声居屋”的名字很可能就源于这个外号。

readings.intro: There are very few personal details here. Thomas, a talented astronomer and ouranoscopist, dispassionately details his observations and the building of the observatory atop the Watchman's Tower.
readings.content: As he records the passing of the Great Comet in 1577, the tone finally becomes more animated but also more obscure. Thomas cites his Dawn Period namesake, Abbot Thomas, as an authority on 'Wind, Moon, and Shell in the Heavens Inferior'. He observes: 'My predecessor knew this Truth - three Blossoms hath the Watchman's Tree: Paper; Ink; and Flame. The Great Comet, I now aver, is that Flame.'

readings_cn.intro: 书中罕有对个人生活的细节描写。作为一名才华横溢的天文学家和窥天术家，托马斯客观而详尽地描述了自己的观测结果，以及在守夜人塔的塔顶建造天文台的过程。
readings_cn.content: 在记录到1577年的大彗星时，文章的风格才终于变得更活泼了些，但同时也更含糊不清。托马斯引用了恰巧与他同名的人物，拂晓时期的托马斯院长的观点——后者是研究“低层天界的风，月，与卵壳”的权威。他评论道：“我的前辈知道这个真理：守夜人之树有三朵花：纸，墨，与火。现在我确证，大彗星正是那火焰。”

items.name: Journal of Walter Dewulf
items.description: Walter Dewulf, 3rd Baron Brancrug, was grandson of Thomas, son of the disgraced Giles, who eloped with 'Pale Hafren'. The Dewulf line might have ended here if the Seneschale Ernestine - by then over eighty - had not managed to reconcile Thomas with a dying Giles.
items.description_cn: 沃尔特·德沃尔夫，第三代布兰库格男爵，托马斯的孙子，耻辱的吉尔斯与“苍白的哈芙伦”私奔后所生的儿子。若非当时年过八旬的欧内斯汀总管设法让吉尔斯在临终前与托马斯和解，那么德沃尔夫家族可能就绝后了。

readings.intro: Walter, though nominally siding with the Parliamentarians, manages to stay out of the war... but in 1642, his son Bryan runs away on the night of his sixteenth birthday and joins the Royalist army. He is captured and returned to his father, who pleads for mercy and gives his parole for his son's good behaviour.
readings.content:
In 1648, Bryan runs away again to join a Royalist uprising. Walter writes of news that Bryan has been seen on the field of battle at Gear Camp, but that his fate is yet unknown. Walter writes one last entry about his fear for his son and the future of his family.

There the journal ends; but the extensive account of Walter's collaboration with the architect Gregory Wheelock includes usefully esoteric information.

readings_cn.content:
1648年，布莱恩再次离家出走，参加保皇党的起义。沃尔特写道，有人在装备营地的战场上看到了布莱恩，而他的命运无人知晓。沃尔特写下的最后一条记录表达了对儿子和家族未来的担忧。

日记到此结束；但关于沃尔特与建筑师格里高利·惠洛克合作的大量记述包含了实用的玄奥信息。
readings_cn.intro: 沃尔特虽然名义上支持议会党，却设法让自己置身于战争之外……可在1642年，他的儿子布莱恩在16岁生日当晚离家出走，加入了保皇党军队。他被俘后被送回了父亲的身边，正是他的父亲为他求情，并为他的良好表现作保，他才得以假释出狱。

items.name: A Pale Lady and a Prince of Wines
items.description: An anonymous biography of Eva Dewulf, last of the Dewulfs, focused rather salaciously on her personal troubles and intrigues.
items.description_cn: 一本关于末代德沃尔夫，伊娃·德沃尔夫的匿名传记，本书更关注她的个人困扰与私密恋情。

readings.intro: Eva Dewulf is engaged to one Abraham Wheelock, but he leaves her at the altar. Furious and humiliated, she returns to Brancrug, and is not seen in London again. Three days after her departure, Abraham Wheelock's body is washed up near Gravesend. His face is so badly pecked by birds that he is only identified by his belongings. These include a waxed pouch containing a letter addressed to Wheelock, whose contents seem to show he is a spy in the pay of the Austrians. Subsequent investigations suggest that the letter is a forgery, but the matter remains obscure...
readings.content: Lord Franklin Bancroft, sometimes called the Prince of Wines, begins a series of visits to Brancrug House. His relationship with Eva becomes a source of scandal. Eva is by now forty-nine, but rumours persist for years of a Dewulf-Bancroft heir. Eva's biographer claims that before her 'drowning death', her child by Bancroft was adopted by her friends the Southeys - that the child became the sister of the later Poet Laureate, Robert Southey. (No real evidence is provided in support of this claim.)

readings_cn.intro: 伊娃·德沃尔夫和亚伯拉罕·惠洛克订了婚，他却在婚礼祭坛前毁约，将她抛弃。伊娃在羞耻与愤怒之中回到了布兰库格，再也没有出现在伦敦。她离开三天后，亚伯拉罕·惠洛克的尸体被冲上了格雷夫森德的海岸。他的面部被群鸟啄食得面目全非，只能通过随身物体来辨认——其中包括一封烫有漆印的、寄给惠洛克的信，信的内容似乎表明他是奥地利人雇佣的间谍。后续调查显示信件似乎系伪造，但事件的全貌依然不甚明了……
readings_cn.content: 富兰克林·班克罗夫特勋爵，有时也被称为葡萄酒王子，他对布兰库格庄园进行过一系列的造访。他与伊娃的关系逐渐成为了丑闻的源头。伊娃当时已经四十九岁，但关于德沃尔夫与班克罗夫特所生后嗣的传言却多年不绝。这本传记的作者声称，在伊娃“投水而死”之前，她与班克罗夫特所生的孩子已经被她的朋友骚赛夫妇收养——这个孩子成为了日后的桂冠诗人罗伯特·骚赛的姊妹（此说法并无实证）。

items.name: A True History of Valentine Dewulf
items.name_cn: 《瓦伦丁·德沃尔夫之真实历史》
items.description: Written in the third person by Valentine Dewulf. Rarely coherent, though it includes some useful footnotes on falconry and on exotic veterinary medicine.
items.description_cn: 瓦伦丁·德沃尔夫在写作时使用了第三人称。本书的脚注中包含了些许关于猎鹰与异国兽医学的实用知识，但行文却杂乱无章。

readings.intro: Valentine is obsessed with the meaning of the Dewulf coat-of-arms: 'On a field or, a chevron enarched gules between two corby heads erased sable in chief and a wolf sejant sable in base.'
readings.content: 'Long have the two birds pursued my blood, yet one is no Crow, yet it is darker. Long has the Wolf rolled itself in gold like a clovered cow, until its slobberings stain our thoughts…'

readings_cn.intro: 瓦伦丁痴迷于德沃尔夫家族的盾形纹章代表的意义：“红底或红色拱山形纹，顶部为两个暗棕色鸦首，底部为蹲坐的暗棕色狼。”
readings_cn.content: “那两只鸟一直都追逐着我的血液，其中一只不是乌鸦，比乌鸦更黑。那头狼一直都将自己裹在黄金之中，就如同沾满苜蓿的母牛，直到它的口水玷污我们的思维……”

items.name: Annals of St Brandan's
items.description: Over a hundred years of the abbey's annals, from 1230 to 1350.
items.description_cn: 修道院从1230年到1350年间合计一百余年的编年史。

readings.intro: Three events of particular interest are recorded: an endowment by Eva de Braose, widow of the Marcher Lord Gwilym Ddu ('Black William), which enables an expansion of the Abbey; the construction of the Winter Tower, which is dedicated to the Madrugad; and the death 'by poisoning and Arts unsanctioned' of Abbess Nonna...
readings.content: After Abbess Nonna's death, the 'double foundation' is dissolved and the monastery is reformed to accept only male novices. At this point the ink changes. The helpful scribe explains that for the new foundation, the Abbot has mandated stargall, not yewgall, ink. He outlines the differences (use of Inks of Containment techniques with a Sky, not Nectar, context) but doesn't trouble to explain why.

readings_cn.intro: 书中记录了三件让人尤其感兴趣的事件：边地领主格威利姆·杜尔（即“黑威廉”）的遗孀，伊娃·德·布劳斯女士，曾捐赠一笔巨款，使修道院得以扩建；献给昕旦的建筑——冬塔的修建过程；以及因“毒药与未经批准的技艺”而遇刺身亡的诺娜院长……
readings_cn.content: 诺娜院长死后，“双重修道院”解体，修道院也改革为只接受男性修士加入。同一时期，墨水也发生了变化。本书乐于助人的抄写员解释道，对新的基金会，院长要求使用星瘿墨，而不是杉瘿墨。他概述了两者的差异（依然使用“收容之墨”技术，但要用穹，而非蜜），但没有费心解释其中的原因。

items.name: The Most Sorrowful End of the Lady Nonna
items.description: An unauthorised account of the death of Abbess Nonna, written by Eusebia, one of the two sisters accused of having murdered Nonna through 'poisoning and Arts unsanctioned.' Eusebia, awaiting execution, intends to hide this account in her cell...
items.description_cn: 一份对诺娜院长之死非官方认可的记录，作者为尤西比亚，被指控使用“毒药与未经批准的技艺”谋杀了诺娜的两名修女之一。等待处决的尤西比亚自述打算把这份记录藏于牢房之中……

readings.intro: Nonna has introduced Eusebia to an unsanctioned Thunderskin-cult which meets in the caves below the Abbey; there she and others perform sacred dances for 'the Preservation of the Kingdom.'
readings.content: Eusebia claims that Nonna asked her and another sister to prepare her a leathy-draught (which can be brewed from another beverage with Herbs and Infusions techniques, and a sufficient quantity of Nectar) for a rite all three of them would perform below the Abbey. Something goes awry, Nonna is 'possessed of a tenebrous spirit', and the Abbey-brethren are forced to 'quell her with star-iron'. The other two are implicated: as scapegoats, Eusebia implies, although she acknowledges her fault also...

readings_cn.intro: 诺娜将尤西比亚引荐给了一支未经批准的、信仰轰雷之皮的异端教派。该教派在修道院地下的洞窟中集会，在那里她和其他人为了“王国的存续”而表演神圣的舞蹈。
readings_cn.content: 尤西比亚声称是诺娜让她和另一位修女为自己调制一份遗忘饮剂（以“草药与药汤”技术配合足够的蜜从其他饮品中调制），用于三人在修道院地下的仪式。但事情出了差错，诺娜被某种“幽暗的灵体”附身，其他教友们被迫“用星辰之铁使她安息”。另外两人也难辞其咎，尤西比亚暗示自己是替罪羊，虽然她也承认自己犯下的过错……

items.name: Three Flowers Hath the Tree
items.description: Ernestine Peterhans records her observations of the growths of trees and flowers around the Isle, and the omens and portents she attempts to draw from them - particularly the yew-tree in Earl Brian's Meadow, whose flowerings are sometimes eccentric.
items.description_cn: 欧内斯汀·彼得汉斯记录了她对岛上树木与花卉生长状况的观察结果，以及她尝试从中汲取的预示与征兆——尤其是布莱恩伯爵甸的那棵紫杉，它有时会开出反常的花朵。

readings.intro: Ernestine observes that in years when the tree flowers black, 'troubling Secrets arise'; when it flowers red, war and fires follow; and that no Dewulf heir has ever been born in a year when it flowers white...
readings.content: Ernestine attempts to use the tree's growths to advantage in her business affairs, but it fails. She is evidently very concerned when Hendrik Dewulf's grandson Giles runs off with 'the Pale Trollop Hafren' in a year when the tree flowers white - she begins to fear she has entirely misinterpreted all the relevant omens. She is deeply concerned for the continuation of the Dewulf line, and prays for Giles' return.

readings_cn.intro: 欧内斯汀注意到，在紫杉树开出黑花的年份，“令人不安的秘密重现于世”；在开出红花的年份，战争与火灾接踵而至；而从未有德沃尔夫家族的子嗣在它开白花的年份出生……
readings_cn.content: 欧内斯汀试图用这棵树的花来预测该年将发生的事情，以此为自己的“事业”谋利，但失败了。亨德里克·德沃尔夫的孙子吉尔斯与“苍白妖女”哈芙伦私奔的那年，紫杉树开出了白花——这让她开始担心自己是不是把所有相关的预兆都搞错了。她明显非常重视德沃尔夫的血脉能否延续下去，并祈祷吉尔斯能够浪子回头。

items.name: The Shadow in the Stair
items.description: Ernestine Peterhans records her conversations with the 'little darkness' in Hush House's Stair Tenebrous, which she calls 'Donkerling'.
items.description_cn: 欧内斯汀·彼得汉斯记录了她与噤声居屋幽暗楼梯中的“小小黑影”之间的谈话，她称它为“鞑喀吕”。

readings.intro: Ernestine's business in the cellars of Hush House often took her up and down the Stair Tenebrous, although it is avoided by every other servant. 'Donkerling' attempted first to consume her and then to demand sacrifices from her; Ernestine consented to bring it mice, but became very stern when it asked for a 'new-drowned child...'
readings.content: 'Donkerling' claims to be an imprisoned Long under the protection of 'the deepest power of the Sea'. It is prone to occasional bouts of raving about how, when it has its freedom, its patron will drown the Isle. Ernestine renders most of these long speeches as '...', but is very interested in what it can tell her about the circumstances of shipwrecks; there are hints that she may have been planning a salvage expedition.

readings_cn.intro: 欧内斯汀因有部分事务需在噤声居屋的地窖完成，经常会需要在幽暗楼梯上下，尽管其他仆人都会尽可能避开它。“鞑喀吕”一开始先是想吃掉她，无果后转而要求她提供祭品；欧内斯汀同意给它带几只死老鼠，但当它要求“刚溺死的婴儿”时，她严厉地回绝了……
readings_cn.content: “鞑喀吕”自称是一名遭囚的长生者，受到“大海最深处力量”的庇护。它偶尔夸夸其谈当它重获自由时，它的庇护者将如何淹没整座岛屿。欧内斯汀对这些长篇大论基本嗤之以鼻，但对它能告诉她的那些关于沉船的消息非常感兴趣；有迹象表明，她似乎曾计划过一次打捞行动。

items.name: Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1927
items.description: Accounts by Governor Collers' private secretary of interventions and experiments in the last years of the Cucurbit prison, focusing particularly on prisoners he believes might have Carapace Cross lineage.
items.description_cn: 典狱长科勒斯的私人秘书对炼金瓶监狱最后几年的干预和实验情况的记述，尤其聚焦于他认为最可能留有介壳种血统的囚犯。

readings.intro: Two prisoners suspected of oneiric crimes are encouraged to access their inner Carapace Cross tendencies, and develop the attributes of the Seglaz-kind ('sickle-formed pseudocrustacea'). Regrettably they lose the ability to breathe air; one dies and Collers releases the other into the sea.
readings.content: Collers describes how he's successfully induced an unstable Carapace-larva to develop into a greater form, using Insects and Nectars techniques in the context of considerable Moon-aspect to 'awaken what would rather remain hidden'. He hopes that similar techniques might be used to expedite the moral development of prisoners...

readings_cn.intro: 两名被控在梦中犯罪的囚犯在科勒斯的刺激下接触到了他们内在的介壳种倾向，并进化出了镰齿族（“镰刀状的伪甲壳类”）的某些特征。遗憾的是，他们失去了在空气中呼吸的能力，其中一人死亡，另一人则被科勒斯放归大海。
readings_cn.content: 科勒斯描述了他是如何成功诱导介壳幼虫的进化，即在相当强度的月相下，利用“昆虫与花蜜”技术“唤醒那些更愿隐藏的东西”。他希望类似的技术可以用来加快囚犯的道德发展。

items.name: Cucurbit Prisoner Records 1928
items.description: Accounts by Governor Collers' private secretary of interventions and experiments in the last years of the Cucurbit prison, focusing particularly on the 'hill-children', wild Wood-things that have found a shape in the physical world.
items.description_cn: 典狱长科勒斯的私人秘书对炼金瓶监狱最后几年的干预和实验情况的记述，尤其聚焦于“丘陵之子”，即在物理世界获得形体的野蛮林地生物。

readings.intro: Something called a 'Singlefoot', a horned mountain-dweller, is brought back from some kind of embassy to the Grove of Green Immortals. Collers expresses his irritation that Gervinus van Lauren refuses to assist in its containment.
readings.content: The Singlefoot somehow conjures an earthquake that cracks the tower and enables its escape. Collers determines that it should not have been permitted to dream while kept beneath the earth: it had access to sufficient Scale aspect to use its 'arts of Hill and Hollow' to develop an Old Moment into an Earthquake Name. He mandates above-ground confinement for all hill-children prisoners in the future.

readings_cn.intro: 一头被称为“夔牛”的有角山地居民被从某个大使馆带回了翠仙苑。格维努斯·范·劳伦拒绝帮忙控制它，科勒斯表示愤怒。
readings_cn.content: 夔牛用某种方法引发了一场地震，震裂了高塔而得以逃脱。科勒斯认为，把它关在地底下时不该允许其做梦：它接触了足够的鳞相，得以利用“丘陵与孔窍之技艺”将“旧日时刻”升变为“震灾之名”。他规定今后所有的丘陵之子都必须被关押在地面之上。

items.name: On the Winding Stair
items.description: Gregory Wheelock, the master mason and architect employed by Walter Dewulf to construct the Winding Stair and the guest chambers in Hush House, describes a more ambitious and dangerous project.
items.description_cn: 格里高利·惠洛克，石匠大师与建筑家，受沃尔特·德沃尔夫聘请建造了噤声居屋的盘旋楼梯与客房，他在本书中描述了一个更具雄心和危险的计划。

readings.intro: Gregory marks the bricks of his Roost-touched family home, Treowen, with Ramsund, hoping to open forbidden doors…
readings.content: Gregory evidently succeeds in opening a way to something he calls the 'Moon-Hall', but here his account becomes erratic. He insists that in the Moon-Hall the Horned-Axe is still an Edge-power; he hopes for an 'eternal rival', but cannot find the one he needs. The narrative is increasingly interspersed with chess notations, and ends abruptly.

readings_cn.content: 格里高利显然成功地开辟了一条通往他所谓“月厅”的通道，但在那之后，他的叙述逐渐越发混乱。他坚称在月厅内双角斧依然是一位刃之神明；他希望能有一个“永恒的对手”，但未能找到。后期的记述中越来越多地穿插着象棋记步的符号，最终戛然而止。
readings_cn.intro: 格里高利用拉姆桑德语在他那为栖木所触的房屋——特罗文的砖墙上做了标记，想要开启遭禁的门扉……

items.name: Letters from a Fugitive
items.description: Lars Westergren, explorer and murderer, spent seven years escaping justice through his knowledge of byways and shortcuts in the Bounds. Throughout that time he wrote regularly to his daughter, possibly in part to taunt his pursuers.
items.description_cn: 探险家及杀人犯拉尔斯·韦斯特格伦曾在七年的时间里，利用他对边境上的小路与边门的了解躲避追捕。在那段时间里，他曾定期给自己的女儿写信——兴许也是为了嘲讽他的追兵们。

readings.intro: A year with the Légion du Seuil, patrolling the Bounds, until he deserts; a month in the Priory of Captains in Morbihan; seven days, or so he claims, in Ys behind the wave…
readings.content: Cornered at last by his pursuers, Westergren writes that he will 'attempt the Paths of the Sun'. He doesn't seem sanguine about his chances, and indeed, this is his last letter. An editor's note adds that Westergren's whereabouts or end remain unknown, although he was supposedly sighted at the 'Christmas Market' in Vienna - the negotiations between invisible underworld figures that happen each year there - in 1929.

readings_cn.intro: 韦斯特格伦曾在门关军团服役一年，巡逻边境，直至叛逃；在莫尔比昂的船长修道院躲了一个月；还在波涛之下的伊苏住了七天（至少他如此声称）……
readings_cn.content: 在最终被追兵逼得走投无路的时候，韦斯特格伦写道，他将“尝试日之道途”。他对自己的冒险行为似乎也不怎么乐观，事实上，这是他的最后一封信。编者在最后补充说，韦斯特格伦的下落与结局依然不明，尽管据说有人在1929年维也纳的“圣诞集市”上见过他——那是无形世界的黑帮人物们每年举办的洽谈会。

items.name: Perugian Diaries
items.description: In 1907, at the age of eighteen, Christopher Illopoly left Strathcoyne's household to study theology at the University of Perugia in Italy, enrolling under the name 'Christopher Strathcoyne'.
items.description_cn: 1907年，十八岁的克里斯托弗·伊利奥波里离开了斯特拉思科因的宅邸，以“克里斯托弗·斯特拉思科因”之名在意大利的佩鲁贾大学学习神学。

readings.intro: For four years, since his adoption from a Bristol orphanage, Illopoly served as Strathcoyne's pupil and protégé, but his relationship with this austere and secretive man was always complicated. His journal confides: 'I still think Fraser's intentions are good. Certainly he agrees. But I never understood the final goal of his investigations. He was never prepared to enlighten me. And good intentions or not, I can no longer bear this dream of eyes. We have agreed to part, almost amicably.'
readings.content: Illopoly left Perugia in 1909 without completing his degree. He had long lost interest in his studies, and the latter half of the journal is concerned with his studies of Umbrian folk-songs, and notes towards his own compositions (which are of widely varying quality). One of the better ones, 'In the Marshes of Night', suggests he visited the site of the old Lake Fucinus near Ortucchio…

readings_cn.intro: 自从被斯特拉思科因从布里斯托尔的一家孤儿院收养后，伊利奥波里在长达四年的时间里都是他的学生与门徒，但是他与这位严肃而神秘的绅士之间的关系总是十分复杂。他在日记中透露：“我依然认为弗雷泽是出于好意的。当然他也同意这点。但我始终无法理解他那些研究的最终目标。他也从不准备开导我。不论是否出于好意，我再也没法忍受眼之梦了。我们还算是友好地分道扬镳。”
readings_cn.content: 伊利奥波里没有完成学位课程，就在1909年离开了佩鲁贾。他早就对自己的专业失去了兴趣，日志的后半部分主要是他对翁布里亚民歌的研究，以及他对自己早期作品的注释（这些作品的质量参差不齐）。其中较好的一篇，《于黑夜的沼泽》，暗示了他曾参观过奥尔图基奥附近的古老富奇诺湖……

items.name: Key of Night
items.description: The deliberations leading to a manifesto of the 'Worms of a Scale', as recorded around 1900 in the Bar Vienna, in the cellar of the Hotel Ciervo in Noon.
items.description_cn: “共鳞蠕虫”宣言的商议内容记录。该会议于1900年左右在位于午港的希耶尔沃旅店地下室的维也纳酒吧中举办。

readings.intro: The Worms, all of whom use grandiose noms de guerre like Citizen Knife and the Midnight Pilgrim, agree that all previous iterations of their movement have been feckless and treacherous, and agree that the return of the prehuman Hours - the gods-from-stone - is the true way to end 'the tyranny of Eternity.'
readings.content: The Worms identify the Wheel, the Tide, the Flint, Sulochana, the Spider Door, the Excellency Gnathobasis and Wickel Inextinguishable as the Seven Necessary Pentiments that must be 'returned to every History through the Propaganda of the Deed'. This is an eccentric list and clearly a compromise; the process of thrashing it out clearly exhausts all the participants, who don't specify the necessary Deed beyond a vague reference to 'the Loopholes'.

readings_cn.intro: 以“公民之刃”和“午夜朝圣者”之类的noms de guerre（浮夸假名）自命的蠕虫派们，一致认同在此之前蠕虫派的所有运动都是无用和背信的，也一致认为前人类时代的司辰——石源神的回归才是结束“永恒的暴政”的真正途径。
readings_cn.content: 蠕虫派把转轮、浪潮、燧石、苏洛恰那、蜘蛛之门、巨颚阁下、“不灭灯芯”维克尔列为“最应该经由行动宣传回归各重历史”的七种必要覆画残迹。这是一份古怪的名单，也显然是妥协的结果；制定名单的过程让所有参与者都精疲力尽。除了含糊地提到所谓的“永恒罅隙”外，他们没有具体说明必要的行动是什么。

items.name: On Resonance
items.description: Experiments in ithastry by the 'sky-smith' Everett Vinzant.
items.description_cn: “天匠”埃弗莱特·文赞特关于盗火术的实验记录。

readings.intro: Vinzant suggests percussion instruments that might be 'sympathetic' to a number of Hours and Names. Some are more likely than others…
readings.content: Vinzant uncontroversially suggests drums of various materials as the sympathetic instrument for the Thunderskin and its 'ascendant duendrazones'. He proposes bells of bronze and iron for the Lionsmith and Colonel. He spends some time on the design of a 'bee-rattle' for the Malachite, but doesn't seem entirely confident of his findings...

readings_cn.intro: 文赞特认为，打击乐器兴许能与司辰和具名者“交感”。其中一些尤其容易做到这点……
readings_cn.content: 文赞特以无可辩驳的语气建议使用各种材质做成的鼓作为与轰雷之皮及其“上位叩心魅”交感的乐器。对于狮子匠和上校，他则分别推荐铜与铁铸成的大钟。他还曾试图为石绿设计一种“蜂鸣装置”，但似乎对自己的发明并没有充足的信心……

items.name: Enchiridion Tragularis
items.description: The poison-manual of the order of assassins called the Tragulari.
items.description_cn: 人称图拉古拉里的杀手组织的毒药使用手册。

readings.intro: The Tragulari - 'dartsmen' - were employed by the Duties in their various incarnations to hunt down inhuman troublemakers. They developed poisons that even the immortals called Long could not withstand…
readings.content: Immunity to their own poisons was a constant concern for the Tragulari, and they constantly dosed themselves with substances that might built up immunity. Perinculate, the notoriously toxic Unsanctioned Ink, can be used as a base for one of these - Serpent-Milk - with sufficient Scale and with arts of Serpents and Venoms.

readings_cn.intro: 图拉古拉里，即“投枪手”，受雇于相关机构，以各种化身来猎杀非人的麻烦制造者。他们研制出了甚至连被称为长生者的不朽存在都无法抵御的毒药。
readings_cn.content: 能否免疫自己造的毒药对图拉古拉里来说始终是个重要的问题。他们不断服用可以增强抗性的药剂。凶匿墨，一种剧毒且未经批准的墨水，再加上足够的鳞与“群蛇与毒液”技艺，便可制成上述药剂中的一种——蛇乳。

items.name: The Republic of Teeth
items.description: An eccentric political tract by Valentine Dewulf.
items.description_cn: 瓦伦丁·德沃尔夫编写的一本古怪的政论小册子。

readings.intro: Valentine suggests that rulers should be elected to govern by serpents, not their subjects, 'for the Serpent, being cold-blooded in its Nature, is incorruptible.'
readings.content: Valentine's initial proposal is that a college of electors should subject themselves to the bites of venomous serpents - which he grades and details, preferring the least dangerous - and should allow the resulting deliria to guide them in their choice of people's representatives. He becomes concerned, however, by the practicalities of ensuring equal quantities of venom in each case, and gets half-way into a proposal for using birds instead in the selection process, before giving up mid-sentence.

readings_cn.intro: 瓦伦丁提议说，统治者应当由毒蛇来选举产生，而不是由他们的臣民，“因蛇天性冷血，不可腐蚀。”
readings_cn.content: 瓦伦丁最初的建议是，所有的选民都应该主动接受毒蛇的啃咬——他在书中对毒蛇进行了评级和详述，推荐了危险性最小的——并让中毒产生的谵妄指导他们选出人民的代表。然而，他开始担心在不同情况下确保使用等量毒液的可行性，作为折中提出了使用鸟类的替代方案——但这项讨论只进行到一半就被放弃了。

items.name: Seven Faces of Icarus
items.description: In the early 1530s, the last Abbot of St Brandan's, called 'Roaring Richard', set down his conversations with the illiterate local cunning-man, Red William.
items.description_cn: 在16世纪30年代早期，圣布伦丹修道院的最后一位院长“咆哮的理查德”记录下了他与当地一名目不识丁的神汉红威廉之间的谈话内容。

readings.intro: Red William describes the seven forms in which he 'goes about and under the world' - viper, cat, fox, eagle, dove, boar and crow. Abbot Richard ingeniously fits these all into a framework of Solar belief…
readings.content: According to Abbot Richard, each of Red William's forms is closer to the Sun, and is increasingly 'winged with virtue'. Richard draws an analogy with the waxen wings of Icarus: hypocrisy and false virtue will melt before the Sun's heat, and so sincerity and untrammelled expression of the Self are the utmost piety. It's worth noting that only a year or two after Richard wrote this book, John Tregonwell was so appalled by the debaucheries of the monks of St Brandan's that he recommended the monastery's immediate dissolution.

readings_cn.intro: 红威廉描述了他“在世界之中与之下游荡”的七种姿态——毒蛇、猫、狐狸、雕、鸽子、野猪和乌鸦。理查德院长将这些姿态巧妙地融入了太阳信仰的框架之中……
readings_cn.content: 根据理查德院长的说法，红威廉的每种姿态都更接近太阳，并且日益“以美德为翼”。理查德以伊卡洛斯的蜡翼与之做了类比：伪善和虚假的美德会在太阳的高温下融化，因此真诚和无拘无束的自我表达才是最大的虔诚。值得注意的是，就在理查德完成本书的一两年后，约翰·特雷贡韦尔对圣布伦丹修道院内修士们的放荡行径大为震惊，责令立即解散修道院。

items.name: On Thirstlies, Ivories and Lovelies
items.description: Fionna Ayrshire recounts her visits in dreams to the 'Red Church' in the Mansus, and her conversations with the Names of the Grail.
items.description_cn: 菲奥娜·艾尔郡在本书中记录了她在梦中造访了漫宿中的“赤红教堂”时的见闻，以及她与赤杯的具名者们的对话。

readings.intro: An Hour, Ayrshire explains, may usually only have seven Names - but since the Thirstlies, Ivories and Lovelies who usually comprise the Red Grail's Names are constantly attempting to devour one another, and the Names of other Hours, that number fluctuates.
readings.content: Lovelies, the 'freshest' of the Grail's Names, usually adopt the characteristics of whatever they devour - be it an Ivory, a Thirstly, or, occasionally, an entirely different kind of Name. A practical application of the principle is described. The arts of Resurgences and Emergences, in the presence of sufficiently potent Grail-aspect, can be used to feed a Pale Mommet to its successor-doll, creating something 'notably more avid'.

readings_cn.intro: 艾尔郡解释说，一位司辰通常仅拥有七位具名者，但由于干渴者，骨白者与美貌者——这三类赤杯的具名者总是会尝试吞噬彼此，或是其他司辰的具名者，所以数量时有波动。
readings_cn.content: 作为圣杯具名者中“最新鲜”的一种，美貌者通常会继承它们吞噬之物的特征——骨白者，干渴者，偶尔也有全然是别种的具名者。书中还介绍了将该原理应用于实际的示例。在足够强大的杯相存在的情况下，“复苏与羽化”技法可以用于将苍白人偶饲喂至进阶形态，创造出“更加贪婪之物”。

items.name: By Their Marks Shall Ye Know them
items.description: A monster-hunting initiate of the Hour named the Colonel, who identifies herself as 'Little Sophia', provides advice on finding the weak spots of Long.
items.description_cn: 作者自称“小索菲亚”，是一位拜入上校麾下，负责狩猎怪物的门徒。她为如何找到长生者的弱点提供了一些建议。

readings.intro: Little Sophia observes drily: 'Should one desire to slay an immortal, it is most practical to do so before they become immortal entirely.' She details the 'Marks', the changes that Long undergo as they abandon their mortal condition.
readings.content: As the Lantern-long begins to abandon its flesh, its skin becomes loose, its bones soften. The Sixth Mark is to be observed thus: when the flesh between finger and thumb can be pulled to the final finger-joint…'

readings_cn.content: “当灯之长生者开始抛弃肉体时，它的皮肤会变得松弛，骨头则会逐渐酥软。第六印记可以这样观察到：当其虎口间的皮肤可以拉到小指关节处时……”
readings_cn.intro: 小索菲亚讽刺地提到：“想要杀死一个不朽者，最实际的方法是在其真正跨入不朽前这么做。”她在文中详细描述了“印记”，即长生者抛弃凡人之身所需历经的变化。

items.name: Oblations in Iron
items.description: A Monster-hunting initiate of the Hour named the Colonel, who identifies herself as 'Little Sophia', records the exhibits she has rendered to the Worm Museum in the Mansus.
items.description_cn: 作者自称“小索菲亚”，是一位拜入上校麾下，负责狩猎怪物的门徒。她记录了那些自己奉献给漫宿的蠕虫展馆的展品。

readings.intro: Little Sophia has never visited the Worm Museum, or even the Mansus, in person, and evidently has no desire to do so. She mixes ink which incorporates the remains of her prey, writes her records in that ink, then burns them before the Colonel's altar…
readings.content: 'It is essential however to permit no drop of the ink thereby obtained to enter any portal of the body, even a break in the barrier of the skin. Should any fragment of the Worm remain viable, it might enter thereby, and the Hunt's ultimate conclusion be melancholy indeed...'

readings_cn.intro: 小索菲亚从来没有参观过蠕虫展馆；她甚至没有直接造访过漫宿，而且显然也根本不想这么做。她将猎物的遗骸与墨水相混合，又用那墨水记录下狩猎的过程，将之焚烧于上校的祭坛前……
readings_cn.content: “而最重要的是，一定不能让制取好的墨水滴入身体的任何开口，哪怕只是皮肤屏障破开的一道小小绽口。若是蠕虫的某些碎片依然存活，它就可能借此入侵，导致这场狩猎的结果变得非常凄惨……”

items.name: Prophecies of Glory
items.description: Religious and patriotic fables collected, or composed, by William Gore.
items.description_cn: 威廉·戈尔收集或创作的宗教和爱国主义寓言。

readings.intro: This is much more sober in tone than Gore's previous 'Wainscot Histories'; evidently he became religious in his later years.
readings.content: Each fable describes the coming of the Second Dawn, when the Hours of the Sun will be united - but in 'Eternity Denied', 'The Vampire Light', and 'The Feast of Rays,' Gore depicts a tainted Dawn which can only be purified by a second Division of the Sun. He insists repeatedly on the dangers and temptations of a false Dawn...

readings_cn.content: 每则寓言都描述了第二拂晓的到来，届时太阳之司辰将合为一体——但在《被斥永恒》《吸血之光》《光芒盛宴》这三篇中，戈尔却描绘了一种只有通过再次分裂太阳才能净化的腐坏拂晓。他反复强调虚假拂晓的危险与诱惑……
readings_cn.intro: 与戈尔的旧作《饰壁史话》相比，这本书的文风更为严肃。显然他在晚年开始信教。

items.name: A Shape in Smoke
items.description: Ambrose Westcott's exposition on tobacco-blending and 'the Oracles of the Pipe.'
items.description_cn: 安布罗斯·威斯考特关于烟丝的调制与“烟斗的神谕”研究的概述。

readings.intro: The text is spotted with spark-holes throughout…
readings.content: Westcott observes gnomically that a pipe might be said to manifest the Red Flower of the Watchman's Tree: 'for when Lies are burnt, Wisdom arises, and vice versa.'

readings_cn.content: 威斯考特铿锵有力地提到，烟斗可能被描述为守夜人之树的红花的象征：“当谎言被焚烧时，智慧自会显现，反之亦然。”
readings_cn.intro: 书中到处都是烟灰烫出来的洞……

items.name: A Light in the Inkwell
items.description: Musgrave, fourth of the Dewulf line, writes tentatively about the 'Covenant of Brancrug' and the legacy of the sacred inks he calls 'encausta revelationia'.
items.description_cn: 马斯格雷夫，第四代德沃尔夫男爵，试探性地谈及了“布兰库格的盟约”，以及一种他称之为“启示之刻”的神圣墨水的某些线索。

readings.intro: 'Words are of the First Importance. So the Book of Suns teaches. But do not Words require Ink? And is the Inkwell not then the Womb of Words?'
readings.content: Musgrave identifies 'the Ichor Auroral' as the mother of the encaustum Porphyrine. He adds that it would be blasphemous to describe the origins of the Ichor itself, although a scrawled marginal note suggests a later reader thought Musgrave was only hiding his ignorance beneath a cloak of piety.

readings_cn.content: 马斯格雷夫认为“曙光灵液”是贵紫之母。他又补充说，描述这种灵液本身的起源是一种亵渎神明的行为，但一条写在边角处的潦草注释表明，一位后来的读者认为马斯格雷夫只是试图以虔诚的外表掩盖自己的无知。
readings_cn.intro: “文字是第一重要的。《骄阳之书》如此教导我们。但难道文字可脱离墨水而存在吗？难道墨水瓶不正是文字的子宫吗？”

items.name: It Is Written
items.description: Musgrave, fourth of the Dewulf line, writes tentatively about the 'Covenant of Brancrug' and the legacy of the sacred inks he calls 'encausta potentialia'.
items.description_cn: 马斯格雷夫，第四代德沃尔夫男爵，试探性地谈及了“布兰库格的盟约”，以及一种他称之为“力量之刻”的神圣墨水的某些线索。

readings.intro: 'As the Light passeth through a Prism into many Colours, so the Great Inks separateth into the Lesser Inks, and the Lesser Inks into Inks Minor…'
readings.content: Musgrave coyly refuses to talk of the Great Inks (or else refuses to admit he doesn't know much about them). He insists that yewgall and stargall, which can be mixed with sufficient Nectar or Sky aspect, are sufficient for 'most befitting Purposes'.

readings_cn.intro: “就如穿过棱镜的光被折射成各种颜色那样，伟大墨水能够被拆分为次级墨水，次级墨水又能被拆分成基础墨水……”
readings_cn.content: 马斯格雷夫委婉地拒绝讨论那些伟大墨水（或者拒绝承认他压根就对其不甚了解）。他坚称在与足够的蜜或穹相混合的情况下，星瘿墨与杉瘿墨能够用于满足某种“最为适当的目的”。

items.name: Ettery After
items.description: An anonymous erotic novel occasionally claimed to have been written by Eva Dewulf, although at least two duels were fought in her honour to avenge this slander.
items.description_cn: 一本匿名情色小说，间或被人宣称是伊娃·德沃尔夫所写，尽管至少已经有两次因捍卫她的名誉而起的决斗是为了报复这类诽谤。

readings.intro: The novel graphically details Madame Ettery's various imprisonments, ravishments and escapes in the debauched Commonwealth of Tinctures and its neighbour, the pious Atrament.
readings.content: It becomes apparent that many of Ettery's lovers and pursuers - Catwink, Houndsgall, Nilique - are transparent allegories for inks, and that Ettery is an embodiment of knowledge pinned to paper - to her mingled delight and dismay. The author only half-commits to the metaphor, though, and is clearly at least as interested in titillation as revelation.

readings_cn.intro: 这部小说绘声绘色地讲述了伊特丽女士在堕落的“染剂”联邦，与它那伪善的邻国“乌墨”所遭遇的一系列监禁、掠夺与逃亡的经历。
readings_cn.content: 很明显，许多伊特丽的情人与追求者——猫瞬，猃瘿，喉青——都是显而易见指向墨水的隐喻，而伊特丽自己则是被固定在纸上的知识的化身；这让她既高兴又沮丧。不过作者似乎只在这些隐喻中投入了部分精力，显然，此人对感官刺激的兴趣至少与其对想要揭露的真相大致相当。

items.name: The Invisible Opera (Unfinished Recording)
items.description: A recording of a 1911 attempt at a performance of 'Wings within Wings', the so-called Invisible Opera.
items.description_cn: 1911年，有人尝试表演了《翼中之翼》（也被称作无形歌剧），此即那场演出的录音。

readings.intro: The singers complete the Skewbald Aria, Beneath Our Skin, and A Rose in Miah without incident; but the Invisible Opera is dedicated to Ferezeref the Magpie, who delights in unexpected interruptions…
readings.content: The recording ends with a clamour of horrified voices, a grating metallic screech, and a soft brass buzzing that fades into burring silence…

readings_cn.intro: 歌手们顺利完成了《花斑咏叹调》，《我们的表皮之下》，以及《弥阿玫瑰》，但无形歌剧是献给“喜鹊”夫里泽里夫的，他偏爱意外的中断……
readings_cn.content: 录音在惊恐的疾呼声，金属摩擦的刮擦声，柔和的黄铜嗡鸣声中结束，逐渐归于寂静……

items.name: Opening the Sky
items.description: An unusual recording of Verro's 'Opening the Sky', composed for the coronation of the New King, Henry IX. The record bears the Suppression stamp EXPUNGE.
items.description_cn: 维罗为新王亨利九世的加冕礼创作的唱片《开启天穹》难得一见的副本。唱片上盖有“抹除”字样的防剿局印章。

readings.intro: The first movement is soft, autumnal. The second unsettling, febrile. The third is bright, soaring, rapturous. The fourth movement is glassy, slithering, a tintinnabulous icicle rattle…
readings.content: The fifth returns to the theme of the third, bright and rapturous once again, but this is a choral movement. It becomes apparent, though, that these are much, much too pure and high to be human voices. They recall birdsong - they recall the sweep of the windswept sky, blue turning black at the edge of the higher heaven - and they wrench the heart in a direction the Bureau does not permit.

readings_cn.intro: 第一乐章轻柔舒缓，秋意浓浓。第二乐章惶惶不安，燥热难耐。第三乐章明亮欢快，高远悠扬，如痴似狂。第四乐章光亮如镜，剔透丝滑，好似冰锥叮铃作响……
readings_cn.content: 第五乐章又回到了第三乐章的主题，再次明亮欢快而如痴似狂，但这是个合唱乐章。不过很明显，这些声音过于纯净高亢，而不似人声。它们让人想起鸟鸣——它们让人想起狂风席卷后的广阔天穹，蓝色在更高远的天界边缘变成黑色——它们将听者的心灵朝着防剿局不允许的方向扭转。

items.name: Lake Fucino Recordings
items.description: Recordings of the folk-dances of the Fucine Marshes.
items.description_cn: 记录了富奇诺沼泽一带的民间舞蹈伴奏的录音带。

readings.intro: The wailing of flutes, the roaring of drums, cries like birds lost in the marshes…
readings.content: These are the songs the Sister sang to the Witch - that the Thunderskin roared to the Sky - the songs with which the duendrazones of the Mansus keep their vigil. Once heard, they are not forgotten.

readings_cn.intro: 笛声的哀婉，鼓声的轰鸣，如鸟儿迷失在沼泽的啼叫……
readings_cn.content: 这是巫女对女巫唱过的歌谣——是轰雷之皮对天穹发出的咆哮——是叩心魅在漫宿时伴其巡逻的乐曲。一旦听过，就再无法忘记。

items.name: Vinzant's Minglings
items.description: The metallurgist and 'sky-smith' Everett Vinzant speaks of 'the sacred alloys', 'the alloys eternal', 'the alloys sufficient', 'the alloys intendant'…
items.description_cn: 冶金学家与“天匠”埃弗莱特·文赞特在本书中谈论了“神圣的合金”“永恒的合金”“必然的合金”与“统治的合金”……

readings.intro: Everett describes the voices and powers of mortals and immortals based on their composition by analogy to the sounds and strengths of bells based on the metals of their casting…
readings.content: Vinzant warns that the mingling of metals of 'too great a nobility' can produce 'the alloys incestuous'. He suggests very cautiously that the means used by the Sovereigns of the Leashed Flame to produce their heirs may have analogous issues: 'for though the Crime of the Sky might be circumvented, yet the Law remaineth the Law, in Spirit as in Letter'.

readings_cn.content: 文赞特警告称，熔炼“过于高贵的金属”会产生“乱伦合金”。他十分谨慎地提出，受控之火的君王用来产生继承人的方法可能也存在类似的问题：“因为天孽虽然可以规避，可法则仍然是法则，无论在灵魂，还是在字面上。”
readings_cn.intro: 文赞特宣称，凡人与不朽者的声音与力量皆基于构成他们的物质，就像铸钟的音色与强度皆基于铸造它们的金属那样……

items.name: Honey: the Comprehensive Guide
items.description: Harvey Hattington - pilot, polymath, confectioner - writes with great enthusiasm about the 'marvellous work of the Bee'.
items.description_cn: 飞行员，传学者兼糕点师哈维·哈廷顿以极大的热情撰写了这本“蜜蜂的奇工”。

readings.intro: Hattington insists that all the primary aspects - Nectar, Scale, Heart, Lantern, Moth, Grail - are possessed by bees and expressed in honey. (Clearly, he points out, there are only six primary aspects, as a honeycomb has only six angles.)
readings.content: 'Yewgall Ink is prepared with these techniques - but so is Skinshuck Mead, and only Skinshuck requires honey. Just as any beverage or foodstuff can be improved with the addition of honey, so any garden is improved with the presence of bees. Even those bloody Blomberende.'

readings_cn.intro: 哈廷顿坚称，所有的基础性相——蜜、鳞、心、灯、蛾、杯——都为蜜蜂所拥有，在蜂蜜中体现。（他也明确地指出，基础性相只有六种，就像蜂房只有六个角那样。）
readings_cn.content: “杉瘿墨就是用这些技术制作的——还有剥皮蜜酒也是如此，且只有后者才需要蜂蜜。正如任何饮品或食品都可以通过添加蜂蜜而得到改善一般，任何花园也都可以通过蜜蜂的存在而得到改善。甚至是那些血腥的绽莓族们。”

items.name: Fekri's Herbary
items.description: The early wisdom of Ehsan Fekri, at that point a travelling healer, much later the Secretary Salvant of the Curia of the Isle.
items.description_cn: 埃桑·费克里的早期作品，早在他担任岛屿决议会的护理理事之前，那时他还是一名旅行治疗师。

readings.intro: As a skaptodon, Ehsan may consume only that which is found in the earth, so he's best with root-lore...
readings.content: Ehsan identifies a pale sea-weed found on the beaches of Cornwall as a useful source of Rose and Winter aspect. His tone here is a little guilty - perhaps because he's showing an interest in sea-produce, which might be thought unwise for a skaptodon, and perhaps because his proposal to name it 'Eva's Locks' suggests a tiny crush on the Pale Lady of Brancrug...

readings_cn.intro: 作为剑齿兽，埃桑只吃在土地中找到的东西，所以他最擅长根之秘传……
readings_cn.content: 埃桑在康沃尔的海滩边发现了一种白色的水草，可作为引相与冬相的实用来源。写到这段时，他的语气似乎有些负罪感——或许是因为他竟然对海产表现出了兴趣，而这对剑齿兽来说是不明智的；抑或是因为他建议把这一物种命名为“伊娃华发”，暗示他对布兰库格的苍白女士有些许好感……

items.name: Kitling Ripe's Tasty Treats
items.description: The Velvet is the Hour of secrets; and so very little is known of the - Moth-long? Nectar-long? - who ascend to immortality under her auspices. But this book (by 'Kitling's Friend') purports to be part cook-book, and part manual for immortality.
items.description_cn: 丝毧是守秘之司辰；所以我们对在她的提携下飞升至不朽的——蛾之长生者？蜜之长生者？——所知甚少。而这本书（作者为“仔猫之友”）的主要内容，一半是烹饪食谱，另一半是追寻不朽的指南。

readings.intro: Kitling Ripe is the name usually given to the speechless 'but never silent' cat-thing that serves as a Name of the Velvet. Kitling Ripe, it seems, enjoys hunting immortals; and the Velvet is very fond of Kitling Ripe.
readings.content: The secret, it appears, is to arouse the Kitling's appetite enough to become her quarry, but not quite enough to be caught. The Velvet permits the game, since it culls immortals careless enough to attract attention, and keeps her Name happy. The author bemoans the loss of the Carapace Cross' savour-secrets, which apparently were particularly tempting - but suggests decent spice-substitutes, which also happen to make for excellent pigeon-pie.

readings_cn.intro: 老成仔猫一般指的是那只无言“但永不沉默”的猫形生物，她是侍奉丝毧的具名者。老成仔猫似乎喜欢狩猎不朽者，而丝毧则十分宠爱老成仔猫。
readings_cn.content: 书中揭露的秘密似乎足以激起仔猫的食欲，变成她的猎物，但不足以被她捕获。丝毧准许这个游戏的存在，因为这既能剔除粗心大意的不朽者，又能让自己的具名者愉悦。作者哀叹介壳种的滋味之秘已然失落，显然，那十分诱人——不过他列出了替代用的其他合宜香料，也恰巧可以用来做一份极好的鸽子派。

items.name: The Barrowchild's Elegies
items.description: The Barrowchild, a Gaulish adept who won a place in the ranks of the Ordo Limiae, enumerates the 'great shadows' laid to rest in tombs of power, and discusses their various conditions.
items.description_cn: “坟茔之子”，一名在利米亚教团中争得一席之地的高卢人学徒，列举了安息在权贵之墓中的“强大阴影”，并讨论了它们存在的不同条件。

readings.intro: The Barrowchild identifies numerous modes that are neither true death nor true life: the 'vitrification of the heart'; 'the corrupt light of the Wood'; 'chor-stasis'; 'the wandering of the fet'…
readings.content: The Barrowchild warns particularly of the 'avidity of trist', where a remnant-shadow's longing for change survives its sense of self and even devours its wist. That longing may draw the curious into the tomb, where the remnant-shadow changes so that it cannot be distinguished from its visitor - or that the reverse becomes true - and that it is never again possible to say whether it is the shadow or the visitor that exits the tomb.

readings_cn.intro: 坟茔之子指出了诸多既非真正死亡，也非真正活着的情况：“心脏的玻璃化”、“林地的腐朽光芒”、“脉律的停滞”、“灵躯的彷徨”……
readings_cn.content: 坟茔之子着重警告了“悲恸的贪婪”：残余的影子对改变的渴望在亡者的自我中保留了下来，甚至会吞噬掉自身的铭晓。这种渴望可能会把好奇的不幸之人吸引到墓中；在那里，残余的影子会发生变化，以至于无法将它与来访者区分开来——或者截然相反——再也无法分辨出离开坟墓的究竟是影子还是来访者。

items.name: Damascene Traditions of the House of Lethe
items.name_cn: 《遗忘家族的大马士革部之传统》
items.description: The House of Lethe was an order of immortals who sought obscurity, rejecting their past and future. If the author of this short text is to be believed, the initiates of the Damascene branch were much more radical than their fellows elsewhere.
items.description_cn: 遗忘家族是由抛弃前尘后事、追求默默无闻的不朽者组成的团体。如果这篇短文的内容是可信的，那么大马士革分部的成员恐怕比他们其他地区的同僚要激进得多。

readings.intro: The House generally forbade any potentially procreative activities, for fear of the terrible consequences of two Long bearing a child. The Damascene order took this much further…
readings.content: At one point, male initiates were required to undergo castration, and female initiates to strangle any children they had previously borne. These measures were so horrific that the Order was shaken by repeated schisms, and eventually absorbed into the local Sisterhood of the Knot as a society of healers and exorcists.

readings_cn.intro: 出于畏惧两位长生者诞下子嗣的可怕后果，遗忘家族通常禁止任何潜在的生育行为。但是大马士革分部的禁令则更进一步……
readings_cn.content: 某一时期，男性新晋者按规定需接受阉割，而女性新晋者则被要求勒死她们之前所生的所有孩子。这些举措是如此可怕，以致于该分部多次面临分裂的危机，最终并入当地的绳结姐妹会，成为了由治疗师与驱灵师组成的团体……

items.name: Exorcism for Girls
items.description: Simple but forceful techniques for 'rousting unbefitting spirits', written in straightforward and colourful language.
items.description_cn: 记载了用于“驱除不合适的灵体”的一系列简单但行之有效的技术，文笔直截了当而生动形象。

readings.intro: Blake seems uncertain at points whether the techniques are intended for use by or on girls. She clearly regards children as a nuisance.
readings.content: Thirza's advice on the shapeless Wood-things known as Raw Prophets is typically practical: (1) discourage them with buckets of water as close as possible to freezing, and with the smoke of dried lemongrass (2) under no circumstances kiss them or receive kisses from them. (3) an effective formula is provided for laundering clothes stained with Prophet-slime.

readings_cn.intro: 布雷克似乎并未明确指出这些技术应该用于女孩们身上还是为女孩们所用。但她明显认为孩子们很讨人嫌。
readings_cn.content: 针对被称为“原生先知”的不定形林地生物，蒂尔扎的建议非常实用：（1）用尽可能冷冻的水和干柠檬草的烟来阻挠它们；（2）在任何情况下都不要亲吻它或被它们亲吻；（3）提供了清洗沾有先知黏液衣物的有效配方。

items.name: Singlefoot Songs
items.description: Father Stanislav John Schaller, priest and diplomat, writes of his time on the slopes of Huashan - 'near to the Grove of the Green Immortals, but never too near.'
items.description_cn: 外交官兼教士斯坦尼斯拉夫·约翰·沙勒神父写下了他在华山山麓度过的时光——“可以靠近翠仙苑，但别靠太近。”

readings.intro: Schaller's relations with the Grove are cautious - it's a Library of the Tree, but under the hand of the Hour named Applebright. In time, however, Schaller comes to be more sympathetic to the Applebright, which he suggests 'causes harm only when so invited.'
readings.content: The 'Singlefoots' of the title are one-horned, one-footed hill-things with sweet but powerful voices - powerful enough to 'open the mountain.' The Singlefoots sometimes trample pilgrims; sometimes heal them; sometimes coerce them to 'enter the mountain' and become Singlefoots. Schaller explains that when he found this last becoming too tempting, he decided to return to his homeland.

readings_cn.intro: 沙勒在处理和林苑的关系时表现得十分谨慎——它是树的图书馆，却处于名为光明果的司辰掌控之下。不过，随着时间的推移，沙勒开始逐渐理解光明果，认为光明果“只在受邀时有害”。
readings_cn.content: 标题中的“夔牛”是一足而独角的山地生物，有着甜美而有力的嗓音，有力到足以“开山”。夔牛有时会践踏朝圣者，有时为他们治疗，有时则强迫他们“进山”而转变为夔牛。沙勒解释说，当发现最后一种情况变得过于诱人时，他当即决定返回故乡。

items.name: An Exorcist's Field Manual
items.description: A practical guide to 'troublesome Dead', grounded in theory but with a clear focus on their disposal, by the redoubtable Detective-Ostiary Wheelock of the Suppression Bureau.
items.description_cn: 一本用于对付“麻烦的亡者”的实用指南，以理论为基础，但明显将重点放在了对它们的清除上。作者是防剿局令人敬畏的司阍侦探，惠洛克。

readings.intro: 'The Dead usually avoid Light - as the most immediate manifestation of Eternity, which has no place for death. However those Dead 'uplifted by gold', that is to say touched by an actinic theoplasma, happily bod about in daylight and are perhaps strongest at noon...'
readings.content: 'If you are dead but 'uplifted by green', that's the Ring-Yew's blessing. (The Crowned Growth offers a similar but nastier benefit.) This is how Burgeoning Risen come about, but there are different degrees of sentience and freedom depending on which growths are involved. The consciousness of one 'uplifted by green' is always greatly altered, though - they never really seem like the same person. They may have dregs of their original souls, but these are often replaced by something else. The upshot, invariably, is that they need to be set firmly on fire.'

readings_cn.intro: “亡者通常会避开‘光’——因为那是永恒最为直接的显现，而永恒中没有死亡的席位。但是那些‘被灿金鼓舞’的死者——换句话说，是被神辉流溢触碰过的那些——能够在日光下欢快地活动，在正午时或许最为强大……”
readings_cn.content: “如果你死后‘被翠绿鼓舞’，那便是环杉的恩赐。（戴冠之孳会提供相似但更糟的恩赐。）这就是抽芽行尸的由来，随着成长程度变化，其将具有不同程度的感知能力和行动自由。不过，‘被翠绿鼓舞’者的意识将发生巨变——它无法再被当作是原来的人。有可能会保留一些原先的灵魂残余，但更多情况下，这点残余也会被其他的什么取代掉。而不变的是，最后总是需要一把火将其烧个干净。”

items.name: Velletri Interviews
items.description: Interrogation of a man named Lacombe, a former Nocturnal Branch inspector now identified as 'terminally robigoid'.
items.description_cn: 对一个名为拉孔布的男人的审讯记录，此人曾任夜勤处的督察，如今则被认定是“晚期罗比戈症患者”。

readings.intro: Lacombe is not especially lucid, and the state called 'robigoia' evidently includes a malady of the lungs which causes coughing fits: he weakens audibly over the course of the interrogation. He is questioned about the disposition of various unsanctioned items recovered from a Nocturnal Branch raid on a castle at Ortucchio, in the region of the Fucine Marshes. He is, however, defiant as well as incoherent.
readings.content: Lacombe insists the items have been put to good use; he derides Nocturnal Branch as 'the lackeys of Calyptra'. Alarmingly, during the last few minutes of the interrogation, he begins to insist that his interrogator should 'burn the Library'. He waxes enthusiastic about the fire he wants to see, leading to a final coughing fit after which the interview abruptly ends.

readings_cn.intro: 拉孔布并不是特别清醒，所谓的“罗比戈症”显然包括某种导致咳嗽的肺部症状。在审讯过程中，他的声音越来越弱。他被质询了对各种未经批准物品的处理情况，这些物品是夜勤处在对位于富奇诺沼泽地区，奥尔图基奥的一座城堡的突击搜查中缴获的。然而，他既态度挑衅，又语无伦次。
readings_cn.content: 拉孔布坚称，那些物品都得到了妥善的利用；他还嘲笑夜勤处是“根冠的走狗”。令人不安的是，在审讯的最后几分钟，他开始坚持审讯者应该“烧掉图书馆”。他对自己想看到的那股火焰充满狂热，这导致了一阵剧烈的咳嗽，审讯在此戛然而止。

items.name: An Investigation of A Foundered Country
items.description: Subtitled 'Recordings from the Atlantic Coast.'
items.description_cn: 副标题是“来自大西洋沿岸的录音带”。

readings.intro: The phonograph initially seems to consist entirely of wave sounds, and the cries of gulls - but attention to the cries suggests they are not gulls at all - perhaps not even birds.
readings.content: The bird-cries resolve to possibly-human voices, half-lost in the sound of waves. They lament the absence of a 'city unborn'; they hymn the 'ice behind the wave,' the 'amber cobbles', or perhaps 'amber corals.' The tenor of their song is melancholy but also, increasingly, menacing, as they promise the 'city irresistible.' As the voices fade, distant bells are clearly to be heard among the surf-sounds.

readings_cn.intro: 最初，播放出的声音似乎完全由海浪声和海鸥的叫声组成——但注意听这些叫声后，听者会意识到那根本不是海鸥——甚至可能不是鸟类。
readings_cn.content: 鸟的叫声逐渐分解成了类似人声的声音，但部分被海浪声所掩盖。它们哀叹“未诞之城”的缺失；它们歌颂“波涛之下的冰城”与“琥珀鹅卵石”——抑或是“琥珀珊瑚”。歌声中的高音忧郁而凄凉，但同时也逐渐变得险恶，因为它们允诺了“不可抗拒的城市”。随着歌声的消逝，能清晰地听到海浪声间夹杂着从远处传来的钟声。

items.name: Recordings from the Althiban Abyss
items.description: Recordings from a subterranean space in the mountains near Baghdad of 'conversations' between the entomologist Juliana Zawistowski and an unidentified presence.
items.description_cn: 昆虫学家朱莉安娜·萨斯托斯基与一个不明存在“对话”的录音带，录制于巴格达附近山体的地下区域。

readings.intro: Only Zawistowski's part in the 'conversations' is comprehensible to the listener. The other side consists of grating, buzzing and rumbling sounds, perhaps only rock movements or artifacts of the recording process, which Zawistowski nevertheless unhesitatingly translates.
readings.content: Zawistowski seems to believe that the presence identifies itself as a Name or remnant of the lost Hour called Seven-Coils. It pleads with her to assist its rebirth; it begs her to find something for it in the city of Emesa. Towards the end of the interview, Zawistowski grows suspicious, and repeatedly accuses the presence of being not the Seven-Coils at all - only 'an inhabitant.' The recording ends in mid-sentence.

readings_cn.intro: 只有萨斯托斯基说话的部分是听者可以理解的，另一头则是刺啦声、嗡嗡声与隆隆声——可能只是岩石运动或者录制过程中人为因素的结果。但萨斯托斯基还是亳不犹豫地将其翻译了出来。
readings_cn.content: 这个不明存在自称是名为七蟠的失落司辰的具名者或它的残余，萨斯托斯基似乎相信了这个说法。它恳请她帮助它重生；祈求她帮自己在埃美萨城寻找一些东西。访谈接近尾声时，萨斯托斯基疑心渐起，并反复指责这个存在根本不是七蟠——只是一个“住客”。录音在此戛然而止。

items.name: Eva's Treasury
items.description: Eva Dewulf, last of the Brancrugs, discusses the occult and aesthetic properties of jewels and other precious minerals.
items.description_cn: 伊娃·德沃尔夫，最后一代布兰库格男爵，在本书中探讨了宝石与其他珍贵矿物在神秘学与美学上的特性。

readings.intro: Black nephrite and scolecite, for Nowhere; orichalc and amber, for Ys; amethyst for the Night Key of the Spider Door...
readings.content: Eva points out - bitterly? - that there is no shortage of uplifting parables and proverbs about the saving graces of a flaw in a jewel; but that no-one, 'not jeweller, not priest, not Hour' has ever found a way to repair such a flaw.

readings_cn.intro: 墨玉与钙沸石，献给虚界；山铜与琥珀，献给伊苏；紫水晶，献给蜘蛛之门的黑夜之钥……
readings_cn.content: 伊娃（苦涩地？）指出——关于宝石瑕疵的可取之处，不乏振奋人心的寓言和谚语；但没有人，“包括珠宝匠、祭司和司辰在内”，找到过能够修复这些瑕疵的方法。

items.name: Advice on Containment
items.description: Thirza Blake discusses ways 'to keep Wood-things out of trouble, and Mansus-things in it.'
items.description_cn: 蒂尔扎·布雷克在本书中讨论了用于“使林地生物远离麻烦，同时让漫宿生物深陷其中”的技巧。

readings.intro: Thirza is irritatingly light on specifics, insisting above all that the duties of an adept are the duties of a host, and that a conjured spirit should be kept in as luxurious a vessel as possible.
readings.content: Thirza notes the similarities between the Lantern-long habit of 'scrining' - returning to the physical world, despite their absence of a body, by entering a mirror or light - and Poemander's techniques of confining Mansus-long to mirrors. She wonders whether Poemander himself might be lured to visit Hush House if provided with a sufficiently alluring scrine.

readings_cn.content: 蒂尔扎注意到了灯之长生者“附体”的特性——尽管它们没有肉体，但可以通过进入镜子或光源返回物质世界——与“牧人者”将栖居漫宿的长生者们困在镜子中的技术的相似之处。她好奇如果提供一个足够诱人的附身物，能否将“牧人者”本人诱来参观噤声居屋。
readings_cn.intro: 蒂尔扎笔下缺少细节的浮光掠影令人恼火。她坚称一名学徒应尽的义务等同于一名主人应尽的义务——换言之，被召唤出的灵体应该被款待于尽可能豪华的容器之中。

items.name: The Admonitory Automata Project
items.description: Footage of experimental devices under development in the Cucurbit under Governor Collers' supervision.
items.description_cn: 记录了在监狱长科勒斯的监督下，“炼金瓶”内部正在开发的实验器材的连续镜头。

readings.intro: The 'admonitory automata' are nasty little things of spring and wire, but they all have merry faces of painted tin…
readings.content: The last item shown is a prototype towards something called a 'condignator', which, Collers says proudly, will allow a prisoner to 'elaborate their own punishment.' He hastens to add that he hopes that in the coming era, 'punishment' will be an entirely obsolete concept.

readings_cn.content: 最后的镜头停留在名为“量刑机”的装置的原型机上。科勒斯自豪地声称它能够让犯人“细定自己的惩罚”。他匆忙地补充到，希望在将来的时代，“惩罚”将会是一个完全过时的概念。
readings_cn.intro: 所谓的“劝诫机”是一系列由弹簧和金属丝组装成的小装置，用途显而易见的恶毒，但都有涂成锡色的滑稽面孔……

items.name: Old Coppernose and the Softer Metal
items.description: A disgraceful compendium of ribald poetry about the habits and corruptions of Henry VIII.
items.description_cn: 一本可耻的下流诗歌集本，描绘了亨利八世的习性与腐败行为。

readings.intro: Henry's 'Great Misfortune' - his crushing injury at a jousting bout - has left him unable to stand 'any straighter than a splintered withy'…
readings.content: The most savage mockery is reserved for Henry's 'Great Debasement', where the corruption of his softer metal is supposed to have crept into the coin of the realm. The last and most serious lampoon makes seditious references to 'the Crucible Revolution'.

readings_cn.content: 嘲弄中最为刻薄的部分针对的是亨利的“大贬质”，他软化金属上的腐败已蔓延到了王国的货币中。最后也是最严肃的一篇讽刺诗煽动性地提及了“熔炉革命”。
readings_cn.intro: 亨利的“大不幸”——他在长枪比武中受的重伤——让他从此无法站得“比折断的柳条更直”……

items.name: Notes on Bindings
items.description: Gideon Dewulf, 5th Baron Brancrug, discusses techniques shared between medical suturing, tailoring, and - carefully, allusively - the binding of restless spirits.
items.description_cn: 基甸·德沃尔夫，第五代布兰库格男爵，在本文中对医用缝合，剪裁缝纫，以及——小心而委婉地提到的——束缚躁动灵体间的共通之处进行了讨论。

readings.intro: Gideon's favourite motif is 'the history of the flesh'. He insists obscurely that histories should be woven, not written.
readings.content: Gideon speaks reverently of the 'wyrd-weft', which he has achieved by applying Stitching and Binding arts to a fabric in the presence of sufficient Winter. He laments however that its complexities only approach those understood by the Sisterhood of the Knot, which in turn are only a shadow of 'the true Braid of Histories'.

readings_cn.intro: 基甸最钟爱的主题是“肉体的历史”。他晦涩地坚称历史应当被编织，而非书写。
readings_cn.content: 基甸虔诚地谈到了“命运纬编”，此物是他在充足的冬下，将“缝合与装订”技艺应用于布料上而造就的。但他还是哀叹道，其复杂程度仅接近绳结姐妹会的理解，而绳结姐妹会又仅是“诸史之真正编结”的一个缩影。

items.name: Hunting Journals of Bryan Dewulf
items.name_cn: 《布莱恩·德沃尔夫的狩猎日志》
items.description: Bryan Dewulf, the son of the 3rd Baron Brancrug, gives advice on hunting in the Bounds.
items.description_cn: 布莱恩·德沃尔夫，第三代布兰库格男爵之子，给出的一些在边境狩猎的建议。

readings.intro: It is clear from Bryan's journals that he sought unorthodox trophies and put them to unorthodox uses. He was in fact hanged as a witch at the age of twenty-four, and never inherited the estate…
readings.content: Bryan describes how a 'Sky-inspired fife' can be prepared using these Fur and Feathers techniques, in the presence of greater Sky-aspect, to 'make of the winds good neighbours.' It's a powerful technique to be described so casually: Bryan's main interest seems to be in ensuring good weather for his hunts.

readings_cn.intro: 从布莱恩的日记中能清楚地发现，他热衷于寻找非同寻常的战利品，并将它们用于非同寻常的用途。事实上，他在24岁的时候就被当作巫师绞死，而且从未继承过遗产……
readings_cn.content: 布莱恩描述了如何运用“毛皮与羽翎”之技艺和“被天穹所鼓舞的横笛”，在强大的穹相下“把风变成友邻”。对于这种如此具有力量的技术来说，他的叙述未免过于轻描淡写：布莱恩的主要兴趣似乎只是以此来确保他狩猎时能有个好天气。

items.name: To a Pale Lady
items.description: A collection of Franklin Bancroft's letters to Eva Dewulf.
items.description_cn: 富兰克林·班克罗夫特写给伊娃·德沃尔夫的信笺集。

readings.intro: There is a substantial body of erotic pleading and half-finished poetry, but also learned discursions on matters mythical and marine, as well as notes towards a comic opera on which Franklin and Eva were apparently collaborating.
readings.content: 'Do not return, O my Light, to the Sea. None of us can be what we were; that is History's curse. None of us know what we may be; that is History's gift. Your mothers, and the mothers of your mothers, are caught in Eternity's jaws like a robe-hem in a trap. It is the pearl that shines; but the tide that returns.'

readings_cn.intro: 书中大量充斥着情色求欢和半成品诗句，但也有关于神话和海洋方面的学术讨论，以及对一部滑稽歌剧的注释，显然富兰克林和伊娃当时正在共同创作此剧。
readings_cn.content: “我的光呵，切勿返回大海。无人能变回我们曾为之物；这是历史的诅咒。无人可知晓我们将为何物；这是历史的赠礼。你们的母亲，以及母亲的母亲，都被永恒的巨口攫获，好似被衣夹夹住的衣角。闪耀的是珍珠；归来的却是浪潮。”

items.name: The Bee-Keeper's Ends
items.description: Dialogues with bees and uses for honey, as erratically recorded by Ricardo Milagro, gardener of Hush House in Musgrave's time.
items.description_cn: 一份关于蜜蜂及蜂蜜之妙用的对话体手稿，作者系马斯格雷夫时期噤声居屋的园丁，里卡多·米拉格罗。

readings.intro: Milagro spends an entire chapter on his hatred of wasps, which he describes as 'the Vile Pretenders'.
readings.content: Milagro claims that bees retain many traditions passed down from earlier and greater branches of their species, but that they are fiercely jealous of these traditions being passed to lesser insects, and insist above all on an oath of secrecy. Tragically, therefore, he is unable to describe these more substantial and powerful traditions.

readings_cn.intro: 米拉格罗用了整整一章来宣泄他对黄蜂的仇恨，他把黄蜂描述为“卑鄙无耻的冒牌货”。
readings_cn.content: 米拉格罗声称，蜜蜂保留了许多从其物种更早、更伟大的支系中流传下来的传统，但它们十分忌讳将这些传统传授给次要的昆虫，并以坚守秘密为要。非常不幸的是，他因此无法描述这些更为基本、更加强大的传统。

items.name: Warming Draughts to Uplift the Heart
items.description: A wonderful compendium of healing tisanes compiled by Natan of Regensburg.
items.description_cn: 一本奇妙的治疗汤药汇编集，作者是雷根斯堡的纳坦。

readings.intro: Natan and his family sought sanctuary at Brancrug but were confined to the Barber's Tower (as it was then known) by the suspicions of the monks, but won more freedom over time…
readings.content: Natan records his delight on the day he was finally permitted access to Earl Brian's Meadow. He speaks very carefully of the black bird he met in its branches, and the 'treasures of music and history' that it brought him when he healed its wing.

readings_cn.intro: 纳坦和他的家人们来到布兰库格寻求庇护，但由于修士们的猜疑，他们的活动范围被限制在理发师塔（后世如此称呼）之内，但随着时间的推移，他们取得了更多的自由……
readings_cn.content: 纳坦记录了他最终获准踏上布莱恩伯爵甸那天时的喜悦。他事无巨细地谈到了那只停在树枝上的黑鸟，以及在为它的翅膀疗伤后，它为他取来的“音乐与历史的宝藏”。

items.name: A Journey to the Grove
items.description: Black Elie, who much later became Damascene Matriarch of the Sisterhood of the Knot, recounts her journey to the Grove of Green Immortals.
items.description_cn: 后来成为大马士革绳结姐妹会头领的黑艾丽，讲述了她前往翠仙苑的旅程。

readings.intro: In the Grove, Elie meets with an entity identified as 'Three Faces, Nine Colours' - who may have become her lover.
readings.content: Three Faces is a Name of the Applebright, the Nowhere Hour of youth, healing and mutation. It offers Elie a form of eternal youth to take back West with her, which she rejects for certain reasons. She does promise, however, to renew their acquaintance 'in the season when the Applebright is the Witch' - not from sentiment, but rather grandly, to ensure the continuity of the Histories.

readings_cn.intro: 在林苑里，艾丽遇到了一个自称“三面九色者”的存在——它可能成了她的情人。
readings_cn.content: 三面者是司掌青春，治愈与变异的虚界司辰——光明果的具名者。它为艾丽提供了一种永葆青春的方法，并让她带回西方，但她出于某些原因拒绝了。不过，她答应会与其在“光明果为女巫的时节”再续前缘——并非感情使然，而是为了更宏大的目标：确保诸史的延续。

items.name: The Hissing Key
items.description: An account of the ascent of the Hour called the Mother of Ants, by the Bosk-scholar Mek, of the Theban branch of the House of Lethe.
items.description_cn: 对被称为蚁母的司辰飞升经历的记述，由遗忘家族底比斯分部的成员，丛林学学者梅克所著。

readings.intro: Mek is not sympathetic to the Mother of Ants, who he calls 'the Milk-Thief'. He reviles her for her part in the death of the Seven-Coils, which he presents as a treacherous conspiracy.
readings.content: The Milk-Thief conspires with the Ligeian Echidna and the Hour-to-be called Chiliarch (now more generally rendered as 'Colonel') to unseam the Seven-Coils with feathers and drown her in salt. The Colonel thus ascends to Hour status; the jealous Milk-Thief, once the Colonel's priestess, seduces Echidna into lending her the Hissing Key to enter the Mansus through the Savage Door, beginning her own ascent to Name and ultimately Hour.

readings_cn.intro: 梅克并不认同蚁母——他称她为“偷奶贼”。他痛斥她参与了七蟠之死的行径，并将之描述为一场奸诈的阴谋。
readings_cn.content: 偷奶贼与丽姬亚厄客德娜、名为千夫长的准司辰（如今更常被称为“上校”）合谋，用羽毛撕裂七蟠，将她溺毙在盐中。上校因此升至司辰之位；而曾是上校女祭司的偷奶贼，因妒羡而唆使厄客德娜借予她嘶鸣之钥，从而穿过狂暴之门进入漫宿，开始她成为具名者，而终达司辰的飞升之途。

items.name: Musgrave's Sketches
items.description: Musgrave, 4th Baron Brancrug, was widely mocked as 'the Bleating Baron' and 'the Lamb Dewulf', but these sketches reveal a complex, sombre inner life.
items.description_cn: 马斯格雷夫，第四代布兰库格男爵，大家都嘲讽他为“咩咩叫男爵”与“羔羊德沃尔夫”，但这些素描揭示了他复杂而灰暗的内心世界。

readings.intro: 'Art begins in Colours; grows Dappled; finally is either mostly Darkness, or mostly Light.'
readings.content: Musgrave discusses the temptation of the perfectly minimal 'palest painting'. He has so far managed to resist this temptation, but does guiltily describe success in using Sights and Sensations with Winter-aspect to create first a 'chilly elixir' from flowers, which he believes he can refine further into a 'final pigment'...

readings_cn.intro: “艺术诞生于色彩；成长于斑驳；最终不是大抵归于黑暗，便是大抵归于光明。”
readings_cn.content: 马斯格雷夫讨论了完美的简约之作“淡白至极的画作”的诱惑。至今为止，他一直都成功抗拒了这种诱惑，但他还是内疚地描述了使用“景象与感知”与冬相，从花中首先制备出一种“冰冷灵药”的成功经验，他相信这种物质可被进一步萃取为“终极颜料”……

items.name: Ambrosial!
items.description: Ambrose Westcott's inventive - one might say pioneering, or indeed buccaneering - essays into kitchencraft.
items.description_cn: 安布罗斯·威斯考特的创作——可称为前卫的，亦或实为冒险的——关于厨艺的论文。

readings.intro: Westcott proudly announces his intention to transform cuisine to become 'an Engine of Alchemy, a Fount of War.'
readings.content: Westcott compares the ferocity of fire with the intensity of appetite as 'in essence, one essence'. A fire's ability to transform and destroy grows when it is offered the correct fuel; so too, he implies, can a sufficiently inspired appetite allow its possessor to consume 'greatly, strangely, unwisely.'

readings_cn.content: 威斯考特将火焰的凶猛与食欲的强烈相比较，“从本质上讲，本质一样”。当提供正确的燃料时，火焰的转化与破坏的能力就能得到增长；同理，他暗示，被充分激发了的食欲也能让它的拥有者“大量、反常、不理智”地大快朵颐。
readings_cn.intro: 威斯考特自豪地宣称，他的目标是让烹饪变成“炼金术的引擎，战争的源泉”。

items.name: Exercises in the Continuity of Self
items.description: Techniques proposed by the Haustorium - the most inaccessible and upsetting of the libraries of the Watchman's Tree - for 'the persistence of memory after the body is discarded'.
items.description_cn: 本书介绍了守夜人之树的图书馆中最难以接近且令人不安的吸器所推崇的技术，可用于“抛弃肉身后记忆的存续”。

readings.intro: The soul-element wist is regarded as 'the fundamental value of the individual'. All other soul-elements, it is implied, may potentially be discarded, as can the individual itself.
readings.content: The Haustorium expresses grudging respect for the Hour called Elegiast, 'who calls each of the Dead by name', but also concern over the Elegiast's subtlety when it chooses to inspire particular interpretations of Histories. The Haustorium proposes the use of Nowhere-energies in distracting or discouraging the Elegiast, in order to assure that 'the persistence of History remains unalloyed'.

readings_cn.intro: 铭晓在本书中被称为代表了“个体基本价值”的魂质。书中暗示其他所有魂质都有被抛弃的可能，就如个体本身那样。
readings_cn.content: 吸器对名为悼歌诗人——“唤亡者以姓名”的司辰表达了不甚情愿的敬意，但也担心悼歌诗人在启发人们对诸史的解读中起到的微妙作用。吸器建议用虚界的力量来干扰或阻遏悼歌诗人，以确保“历史之存续纯粹依旧”。

items.name: The Amalgam of the Red Rose
items.description: An account by 'Mistress Red-Flower' of the alchemical operations favoured by the House of Lancaster, also identified with the 'Sunset Road'. These operations ultimately led to their victory in the War of the Roads, but are described as 'now debased'.
items.description_cn: 作者“红花女士”在本书中讲述了受兰开斯特家族青睐的，又名“日落之路”的炼金学技艺。这些技艺使他们在路权战争中取得最终胜利，却又被描述为“现已衰落”。

readings.intro: The generals of the Houses of Lancaster and York are described as 'brother-enemies' - a term more usually associated with the dyadic, invariably twinned Edge-long…
